xs: The incorrect statement: he arrived on the **eastern coast** — option **(2)**.
**Vasco da Gama** reached **Calicut** (**Kozhikode**) on the **western coast**.
He arrived on **20 May 1498** and was welcomed by the **Zamorin (Samuthiri)** — options 1, 3 and 4 are true.
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: some notes give **17 May 1498**; APPSC-GS **2019** key uses **20 May 1498**.
He left **Lisbon** on **8 July 1497**, sponsored by **King Manuel I**.
He was guided to Calicut by the trader **Abdul Majid**.

150.s: Which of the following pairs about the Treaty of Tordesillas is correctly matched?
o: Lands east of the meridian – Spain
Reference point of the meridian – Cape of Good Hope
Lands west of the meridian – Portugal
150.x: The 1494 treaty fixed a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands, with the east going to Portugal and the west to Spain.
xa: It followed the papal bull **Inter caetera** (**1493**) of **Pope Alexander VI**.
⚠ **1494** Tordesillas sits between **1492** Columbus and **1498** da Gama.

150.s:
Consider the following statements about Vasco da Gama's voyages:
1. King Manuel I of Portugal commissioned Vasco da Gama's expedition that sailed from Lisbon in July 1497.
2. During Vasco da Gama's second voyage (1502), after the Zamorin refused trade, the Portuguese settled at Kochi.
3. Vasco da Gama's third voyage to India in 1524 is associated with his meeting with Jahangir at Surat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
150.x:
Statement 1: Correct: King Manuel I commissioned the expedition, and the fleet sailed from Lisbon on 8 July 1497.
Statement 2: Correct: the Zamorin refused trade, Calicut was occupied, and the Portuguese settled at Kochi.
Statement 3: Incorrect: in 1524 Vasco da Gama returned as Viceroy and died at Kochi; it is not associated with a meeting with Jahangir.

150.s: Which of the following pairs of contemporaries and their positions in 1498 is correctly matched?
o: Immadi Narasimha Raya — Sultan of Delhi
150.x: Manuel I was the ruler of Portugal in 1498. The Zamorin ruled Calicut, Sikandar Lodi ruled Delhi and Immadi Narasimha Raya was associated with Vijayanagara.
150.tq: Avoid swapping contemporaneous rulers across regions.
xs: **Manuel I — King of Portugal** is correct — option **(1)**.
The **Zamorin** ruled **Calicut**; **Sikandar Lodi** ruled **Delhi**; **Immadi Narasimha Raya** ruled **Vijayanagara**.
xa: Manuel I sponsored da Gama's voyage.
⚠ CGPSC 2022: only "Zamorin ruled Calicut" was correct.

150.s: Who guided Vasco da Gama from the African coast to Calicut according to the account of his first voyage?
150.x: The trader Abdul Majid is identified as the guide who helped Vasco da Gama reach Calicut from Malindi. The name also appears in variant form as Majid or Najit in some accounts; the old identification with the Arab navigator Ahmad ibn Majid is doubted, as the pilot was a Gujarati supplied by the ruler of Malindi.
150.tq: Discriminate the navigator's guide from members of the expedition.
xs: The trader **Abdul Majid** guided da Gama to **Calicut (Kozhikode)** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Paulo da Gama** commanded the **São Rafael**; **Nicolau Coelho** the **Berrio**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes give the guide's name as **Najit**.
Route: **Lisbon - Cape of Good Hope - East African coast - Calicut**.

150.s: The statement “the commerce of India is the commerce of the world” is attributed to:
o: Mehmed II of the Ottoman Empire
150.x: The statement is attributed to Peter the Great of Russia and reflects the perceived global importance of Indian commerce.
150.tq: Match the quotation with its speaker rather than its historical context.
xs: "The commerce of India is the commerce of the world" = **Peter the Great of Russia** (APPSC-G2 2017) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Prince Henry** promoted navigation; **Manuel I** sponsored da Gama; **Mehmed II** captured Constantinople.
xa: **Indian textiles** were in huge demand in Europe.
Spices sold in Europe at **60 times** the cost.

150.s: Brazil's Nelore cattle are associated with which place in Andhra Pradesh?
150.x: Brazil's Nelore cattle take their name from Nellore in Andhra Pradesh and make up about 80 per cent of Brazil's livestock.
xa: **Machilipatnam** = Europeans' **first Andhra port**.
The link was recalled with India-Brazil ties at the **17th BRICS Summit** (Jul **2025**).
150.fixed: options 2 and 3 were the same place (Masulipatnam = Machilipatnam)

150.s: Who said the following about 18th century India, "Bear in mind that the commerce of India is the commerce of the world"?
The earliest Europeans to land on Indian soil re were the
150.x: Vasco da Gama's arrival at Calicut in 1498 marked the Portuguese as the first European power to establish a direct sea route to India.

150.s: When did Portuguese admiral Vasco da Gama come to Calicut?
150.x: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama arrived at Calicut (Kozhikode) on the western coast of India in 1498. His arrival opened the sea route between Europe and India, marking the beginning of European maritime trade in the Indian Ocean.

150.s:
Consider the following events :
1. Reign of Krishna Deva of Vijayanagara
2. Construction of Qutub Minar
3. Arrival of Portuguese in India
4. Death of Firuz Tughluq The correct chronological sequence of these events is :
150.x: The correct sequential order is 2, 4, 3, 1. The construction of Qutub Minar was started by Aybak and completed by Iltutmish, the death of Firuz Tughluq in India in 1388 A.D., the arrival of Portuguese (Vasco-da-Gama) in 1498 A.D. and the reign of Krishnadeva Raya of Vijayanagara from 1509 to 1529 AD is the correct chronological order. So, option (a) is the correct answer.

150.s: Who was the first Portuguese Viceroy in India?
150.x: 6. Who among the following had welcomed Vasco da Gama at Calicut? (a) Gasper Correa (b) Albuquerque (c) Zamorin (d) Don Ahnaida U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2013 Ans. (c) 7. Who among the following visitors to India did not belong to Portuguese country? (a) Duarte Barbosa (b) Domingo Paes (c) Peter Mundy (d) Fernao Nuniz U.P.R.O./A.R.O. (Pre.) 2021 Ans (c) Peter Mundy was a 17th century British traveller who came to India during the Mughal rule (Shah Jahan).

151.s: Which of the following is the correct chronological order of arrival of European powers in India?
151.x: Portuguese (1498), Dutch (Masulipatnam 1605), English (Surat farman 1613), Danes (Tranquebar 1620) and French (Surat 1668); the English-before-Dutch order reflects company formation, not arrival.
xa: Order of company formation: Portuguese **1498**, English **1600**, Dutch **1602**, Danes **1616**, French **1664**.
Some notes list Danes before the English — the company years (**1600** vs **1616**) support the standard order.
**FIRST/LAST:** the Portuguese were the first to come and the last to leave (**1961**).

151.s:
Consider the following statements about European trading companies:
1. The Dutch East India Company, established in 1602, was granted sovereign powers such as waging war, building forts and making treaties by the States-General.
2. The French established their first factory in India at Surat in 1668.
3. The English East India Company was formed before the Dutch, Danish and French companies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
151.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the States-General granted the VOC sovereign powers, including making war, constructing forts and concluding treaties.
Statement 2: Correct: the French first factory was at Surat in 1668; the Dutch began at Masulipatnam in 1605 and the Danes at Tranquebar in 1620.
Statement 3: Correct: the order of formation was English (1600), Dutch (1602), Danish (1616) and French (1664).

151.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
151.x: Pulicat became the Dutch headquarters in 1610, later being replaced by Nagapatnam. The French headquarters was Pondicherry, while Tranquebar was the initial Danish headquarters.
151.tq: Start from the distinctive headquarters fact and eliminate swapped locations.
xs: **Dutch — Pulicat** as headquarters from **1610** is correct — option **(1)**.
The **French** headquarters was **Pondicherry**, not Surat (Surat was only their first factory, **1668**).
**Serampore** was Danish from **1755**, not **1616** (the year the Danish company was formed); Tranquebar was their base.
The Portuguese headquarters was **Goa** (Cochin earlier), not Calicut.
xa: The Dutch later shifted their headquarters to **Nagapatnam**.
**Pulicat** was a **Portuguese** settlement captured by the **Dutch**; known for **pepper and cloth**.
Danes sold **Serampore and Tranquebar** to the British in **1845**.

151.s:
Consider the following statements about early European trade in India:
1. The charter of the English East India Company (31 December 1600) was granted by Charles II.
2. Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese at Swally, and the English obtained the Surat farman in 1613.
3. Pulicat was important in the European trade network as the French headquarters and a centre for indigo.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
151.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the charter was granted by Elizabeth I, not Charles II.
Statement 2: Correct: Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese at Swally in 1612, and the English obtained the Surat farman in 1613.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Pulicat was a Portuguese settlement captured by the Dutch that became the Dutch headquarters in 1610, not a French headquarters.

151.s: Which of the following best explains an important reason for the ultimate success of the British in India?
o: The British relied exclusively on naval power and did not use Indian alliances.
The British avoided all involvement in the internal disputes of Indian rulers.
The English East India Company was a private joint-stock company with steady finance and exploited rivalries among Indian rulers.
The English East India Company was directly financed and administered by every Indian ruler.
151.x: The British benefited from the steady finances of a private joint-stock company and from using the rivalries among Indian rulers.
151.tq: Choose the option that combines both stated causal factors without an extreme claim.
xs: The EIC was a **private joint-stock company with steady finance** and **used Indian rulers' rivalries** — option **(3)**.
So the options denying use of Indian alliances or rivalries are wrong.
xa: The EIC was run by a **Court of Directors**.
The **Portuguese** naval monopoly was ended by the **Dutch and English**.
**Wandiwash (1760)** sealed the English victory over the French.

151.s:
Consider the following statements about the Portuguese in India:
1. The rise of the Dutch and English as competing maritime powers most directly marked the end of the Portuguese naval monopoly in the Indian Ocean.
2. The Portuguese first factory at Calicut was established in 1503.
3. The treaty negotiated by Friar Luis with Krishnadevaraya during 1509–10 was associated with the Mughal capture of Hugli.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
151.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Portuguese naval monopoly ended with the emergence of the Dutch and English as competing maritime powers.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the first factory at Calicut was set up in 1500 under Cabral; 1503 is the Cochin fort.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Friar Luis's negotiations were associated with the Portuguese capture of Goa with help from Timmaju, not the Mughal capture of Hugli.

151.s: Blue Water Policy Veeresalingated with
151.x: The " Blue Water Policy " (Cartaz system) was a Portuguese maritime strategy asserting claimed monopoly control over Indian Ocean trade routes, requiring non-Portuguese ships to purchase safeconduct passes, associated with Afonso de Albuquerque's naval-dominance strategy.

151.s:
Consider the following statements about Portuguese governors in India:
1. Afonso de Albuquerque formulated the Blue Water Policy in Portuguese India.
2. The transfer of the Portuguese headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530 was not associated with Afonso de Albuquerque.
3. Afonso de Albuquerque reversed Almeida's naval policy and pursued territorial conquest, including Goa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
151.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the Blue Water Policy was followed by Francisco de Almeida, the first Portuguese viceroy, not Albuquerque.
Statement 2: Correct: Nuno da Cunha moved the headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530; Albuquerque captured Goa, encouraged mixed marriages and abolished Sati.
Statement 3: Correct: Albuquerque reversed Almeida's exclusively naval approach and took Goa, Malacca and Hormuz.

151.s:
Consider the following statements about European settlements in India:
1. The Portuguese obtained Diu in 1535 from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat.
2. Bheemunipatnam in North Coastal Andhra was a Dutch settlement.
3. The Battle of Swally, fought near Surat in 1612, was fought between the English and the Portuguese.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
151.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Diu came from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat in 1535; Goa was taken from the Bijapur Sultan in 1510.
Statement 2: Correct: Bheemunipatnam was a Dutch settlement; Yanam was French.
Statement 3: Correct: at Swally in 1612, the English under Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese near Surat.

151.s: Which of the following statements about the transfer of Bombay is correct?
o: It was received by Charles II as the dowry of Catherine of Braganza in 1661 and transferred to the Company in 1668.
It was received by the Company as a dowry in 1668 and transferred to Charles II in 1661.
It was acquired from the Portuguese by the Company in 1600 without Crown intervention.
It was transferred to the Company in 1757 after the Battle of Plassey.
151.x: Bombay formed part of Catherine of Braganza’s dowry to Charles II in 1661 and was transferred by the Crown to the Company in 1668.
151.tq: Separate the dowry year from the Company-transfer year and identify the correct sequence of ownership.
xs: Bombay was the **1661** dowry of **Catherine of Braganza** to **Charles II**, and passed to the Company in **1668** — option **(1)**.
The Company got it at a **nominal rent** from the Crown; option 2 reverses the order.
**1600** is the EIC charter year — Bombay was not acquired then.
xa: **Madras:** Fort St. George, **1639** (**Francis Day**).
**Calcutta:** Job Charnock at Sutanuti **1690**; **Fort William 1700**.
English headquarters moved from **Surat** to Madras / Bombay / Calcutta.

151.s:
Consider the following statements about early English settlements:
1. Francis Day obtained the site for Madras from the Raja of Chandragiri and built Fort St. George in 1639.
2. Fort William at Calcutta was built in 1717.
3. The farman issued by Farrukhsiyar in 1717 granted the English East India Company duty-free trade in Bengal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
151.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Francis Day obtained the site from the Raja of Chandragiri and built Fort St. George at Madras in 1639.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Fort William was built in 1700, not 1717.
Statement 3: Correct: Farrukhsiyar's farman of 1717 granted the Company duty-free trade in Bengal.

151.s:
Consider the following statements about early English trade concessions:
1. Thomas Best led the English victory over the Portuguese at Swally in 1612.
2. Sir Thomas Roe's mission to Jahangir in 1615 resulted in a formal treaty and the transfer of Bombay to the Company.
3. The Golden Farman of 1636 granting English trade concessions was issued by Abdullah Qutb Shah of Golconda.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
151.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Thomas Best led the Swally victory; Edward Terry was Roe's chaplain.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Roe concluded no treaty with Jahangir; his mission led to factories at Agra, Ahmedabad and Broach.
Statement 3: Correct: Abdullah Qutb Shah of Golconda issued the Golden Farman in 1636, granting trade concessions to the English.

151.s:
Consider the following statements about European conflicts in India:
1. The Battle of Wandiwash (1760) was fought between the English under Thomas Best and the Portuguese.
2. Goa, Daman and Diu were liberated from Portuguese rule in 1961 through Operation Polo.
3. The Marathas captured Salsette and Bassein from the Portuguese in 1739.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
151.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Wandiwash was fought between the English under Eyre Coote and the French under Lally; Thomas Best fought the Portuguese at Swally in 1612.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Goa, Daman and Diu were liberated in 1961 through Operation Vijay, not Operation Polo.
Statement 3: Correct: the Marathas took Salsette and Bassein in 1739, though the Portuguese held Goa against them in 1798.

151.s:
Consider the following statements about the Portuguese legacy in India:
1. The Portuguese cartaz system was primarily a system of naval passes controlling maritime trade.
2. Rubber was introduced in India by the Portuguese.
3. The first printing press in India was introduced by the Portuguese at Goa in 1556.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
151.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the cartaz was a naval-pass system used to regulate shipping and enforce the Portuguese maritime monopoly.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the Portuguese introduced New World crops such as tobacco, potato, chilli and cashew, not rubber.
Statement 3: Correct: the Portuguese introduced the printing press at Goa in 1556.

151.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
151.x: The Portuguese were called Budata Keechu by local people. Bangaru Farmana was the Golden Farman, and Pulicat became the Dutch headquarters.
151.tq: Test the local name and distinguish it from the grant and headquarters terms.
xs: **Portuguese — 'Budata Keechu'** is correct — option **(1)**; it is what locals in **Andhra** called them.
**'Bangaru Farmana'** is the **Golden Farman (1636)** to the **English**, not the Dutch.
**Pulicat (1610)** was the **Dutch** headquarters, not English.
xa: Portuguese influence in Andhra faded by the mid-**17**th century.
Golden Farman issued by **Abdullah Qutb Shah**.
**Yanam** was **French**.

151.s: According to the APPSC examination key, the first European factory in Andhra was established by the:
151.x: The APPSC key identifies the Portuguese as the founders of the first European factory in Andhra at Machilipatnam. Other accounts identify a Dutch factory at Masulipatnam in 1605, so the examination convention must be noted.
151.tq: Distinguish the APPSC key from an alternative account concerning the first Andhra factory.
xs: The APPSC key names the **Portuguese at Machilipatnam** as the first European factory in Andhra — option **(3)**.
This was the **APPSC G2 2019** key.
⚠ Some notes say the **Dutch** set up the first factory (Masulipatnam **1605**) and the Portuguese came last (**1670**) — **follow the key** in APPSC.
xa: **Masulipatnam:** busiest Coromandel port, **textiles**; later English and French too.
**Pulicat:** Portuguese, captured by the Dutch (HQ **1610**).
Portuguese influence faded by the mid-**17**th century (religious intolerance alienated Golconda).

151.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Blue Water Policy – Portuguese naval and trading supremacy
Alauddin's market policy – Portuguese naval supremacy
Home Rule Movement – Boycott of foreign goods
151.x: The Blue Water Policy sought Portuguese naval and trading supremacy; Alauddin's market policy controlled prices to maintain a large army, Swadeshi meant boycott and Home Rule sought self-government.
n: Swadeshi Movement promoted the boycott of foreign goods. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
Swadeshi Movement promoted indigenous goods. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
Home Rule Movement aimed at self-government for India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
Alauddin's Market Policy aimed to control prices. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
Alauddin's Market Policy supported the maintenance of a large army. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
Blue Water Policy aimed at Portuguese naval and trading supremacy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
xa: The Blue Water Policy was introduced by **Almeida** (**1505-09**), the first viceroy.
⚠ Not Albuquerque, Cabral or da Cunha (APPSC-G2 **2023** and **2025**).
**Cartaz** = naval pass; **Caes** = convoy — maritime monopoly tools.

151.s: With reference to the entry of European powers into India, which one of the following statements is not correct?
o: The English opened their first factory in South India at Masulipattam
In Eastern India, the English Company opened its first factory in Orissa in 1633
Under the leadership of Dupleix, the French occupied Madras in 1746
151.x: Option (a) is the correct answer: With the help of the emperor of Vijayanagar, Albuquerque attacked and captured Goa from the Sultan of Bijapur in 1510. All other options are factually correct: In 1611, the English started trading at Masulipatnam and later established a factory there in 1616. The English opened their first factory in the South at Masulipatam in 1611 (Temporary). In Eastern India, the English Company opened its first factory at Balasore in Orissa in 1633 and Hugli in Bengal in 1651. Immediately on its arrival, Dupleix, the French Governor-General at Pondicherry, occupied Madras in 1746 and thus began the First Carnatic War (Anglo-French War) (1746-48).

151.s: At which one of the following places in India did the Portuguese build their first fortress?
151.x: The first Portuguese fortress was built by Afonso-de- Albuquerque (during his first visit to India) in Cochin in 1503. Francisco de Almeida constructed the Portuguese fortress in Cannanore and Anjediva in 1505.

151.s: With reference to the entry of European powers into India, which one of the following statements is not correct?
o: The English opened their first factory in South India
In Eastern India, the English company opened its first
Under the leadership of Dupleix, the French occupied
151.x: The Portuguese Viceroy Albuquerque captured Goa from the Sultan of Bijapur in 1510 A.D. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

151.s: The first to start a joint stock company to trade with India were :
151.x: The First joint stock company for trade with India was the English East India company, established in London in 1600 A.D. After this, a Joint Dutch East India company was established by a resolution passed by the Dutch parliament in 1602 A.D. Since Britain is not in the question option, the answer will be option (b).

151.s: Bombay was taken over by the English East India Company from –
151.x: Bombay was given as a dowry gift by the Portuguese Crown to the British when Charles II, under the marriage treaty of 1661 A.D., the King of England married Catherine of Braganza, the Princess of Portugal in 1662 A.D. Charles II gave Bombay to British East India Company on 10-pound annual rent in 1668.

151.s: Who was the real founder of Portuguese power in India?
151.x: The real founder of Portuguese power in India was Albuquerque (1509-15 A.D.). He established Portuguese State as a powerful regional power in India. The annexation of Goa from the Sultan of Bijapur in November, 1510 was the first significant achievement of Albuquerque. The victory at Goa consolidated the Portuguese monopoly on the southern-western naval coast and established a regional Portuguese State in India. He encouraged Portuguese men to marry Indian women for enhancement of the Portuguese presence in India and the formation of permanent colonies.

151.s: Where in India did Britishers set up their first factory in 1613?
151.x: Captain William Hawkins came to India in 1608 and reached Mughal Court from Surat in April 1609 AD but did not succeed in getting permission to set up a factory. Despite Portuguese antagonism, Captain Middleton landed at Swally near Surat and succeeded in getting permission for trade from the Mughal Governor in 1611 A.D. Captain Thomas Best in 1612 A.D. dissolved the Portuguese monopoly with the victory at Swally. Consequently, the British established a permanent factory in 1613 A.D. They later expanded their trade to other parts of India and established cooperative factories in Ahmedabad, Burhanpur, Ajmer and Agra.

151.s: Which British ambassador came behind Jahangir from Ajmer to Mandu ?
151.x: Thomas Roe arrived in Mughal court in 1616 A.D. He got the opportunity to visit Mandu, Ahmedabad, Ajmer, etc. with the emperor. He went with the emperor for hunting.

151.s:
The following European Powers entered into Indian trade at one time or the other :
1. The English
2. The Dutch
3. The French
4. The Portuguese
Select the correct chronological order of their entry from the code given below :
151.x: The sequence of the arrival of European powers in India is as follows. Portuguese-Dutch-English--Danes-French.

151.s:
Consider the following fruits:
1. Papaya
2. Pineapple
3. Guava
How many of the above were introduced in India by the Portuguese in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries?
151.x: The Portuguese introduced several new crops and fruits to India, including potatoes, sweet potatoes, tobacco, pineapples, cashew nuts, maize, capsicums, papayas, sapodillas, and guavas.

151.s: Which of the British officials defeated Portuguese at Swally?
151.x: Captain Thomas Best defeated Portuguese in 1612 A.D. in the naval battle of Swally near modern Surat city.

151.s: Who were the first Europeans to come to India for trade?
151.x: The Portuguese were the first Europeans, who came to India during medieval period for trade. The first Portuguese and European voyager Vasco da Gama reached the coast of Calicut in 1498 AD after a long voyage with the help of a Gujarati route guide. The sequence of the arrival of the European trade powers in India is as follows: Portuguese, the Dutch, the English, the Danes and French. Portuguese came to India in 1498 and returned in 1961 (longest period).

152.s:
Consider the following statements about Portuguese rule in India:
1. In the Battle of Diu fought in 1509, Almeida defeated the combined fleet of the English, the Persians and Bijapur.
2. The Goa Inquisition used state machinery for conversions and acted against religious dissent.
3. Nuno da Cunha was the first Portuguese Viceroy in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
152.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: at Diu in 1509 Almeida defeated the combined fleet of Gujarat, the Egyptian Mamluks and the Zamorin.
Statement 2: Correct: the Goa Inquisition in the sixteenth century acted against religious dissent and used state machinery for conversions.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Francisco de Almeida, not Nuno da Cunha, was the first Viceroy.

152.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Wheat — Portuguese New World crop introduced into India
152.x: Tobacco, chilli and tomato (to Telugu soil) are Portuguese introductions. Wheat is the wrong pair: it is not a New World crop and is not among the crops the Portuguese introduced.
152.tq: Find the item outside the specified crop group.
xs: **Wheat** is the wrong pair — it is not among the Portuguese New World crops — option **(4)**.
Portuguese crops: **tobacco**, potato, lady's finger, **chilli**, pineapple, sapota, groundnut.
**Tomato** was introduced to **Telugu soil** (APPSC-G2 **2025** key).
xa: **Printing press (1556)**; Bible printed in **Kannada and Malayalam**.
**Vindaloo** comes from **vinha d'alhos**.
New World crops **reshaped Indian cuisine**.

152.s:
Consider the following statements about Portuguese possessions in India:
1. The Portuguese, the first Europeans to come to India, finally left India in 1961.
2. The Portuguese obtained Daman by treaty in 1534.
3. Daman was the Portuguese settlement granted by Akbar in 1579.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
152.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Portuguese were the last European power to leave, in 1961.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Daman was obtained in 1559; 1534 is when Bassein was obtained.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Akbar granted the Portuguese Hugli, not Daman, in 1579.

152.s: Which of the following pairs about the Portuguese on the Andhra coast is correctly matched?
o: Machilipatnam factory of 1670 – Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah
Cause of their decline – Religious tolerance
Waning of Portuguese influence – Early 16th century
Machilipatnam factory of 1670 – Abdullah Qutb Shah
152.x: The 1670 Machilipatnam factory was permitted by Abdullah Qutb Shah; Portuguese influence waned by the mid-17th century as their religious intolerance alienated Golconda.
xa: **Pulicat** was a pepper and cloth centre before the Dutch took it.
Locals in Andhra called the Portuguese **Budata Keechu**.
The Portuguese introduced the **tomato** to Telugu soil (APPSC-G2 **2025**).

152.s:
Consider the following statements about the Portuguese in India:
1. The constant conflict between the Portuguese and the Zamorin of Calicut was mainly caused by Portuguese monopoly and heavy duties.
2. The remains of St. Francis Xavier, who reached Goa in 1542, are preserved in the Basilica of Bom Jesus, Goa.
3. The Portuguese set up the first printing press in India at Goa in 1556.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
152.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Portuguese trade monopoly and heavy duties led to continuing conflict with the Zamorin of Calicut.
Statement 2: Correct: Xavier's remains are at the Basilica of Bom Jesus, Goa.
Statement 3: Correct: the printing press came to Goa in 1556.

152.s: The Portuguese Cartaz system was supported by convoy arrangements known as:
152.x: The Cartaz system was backed by the Caes convoy system and customs duties, and was used in the Bay of Bengal too.
xa: Every Indian Ocean ship had to buy one; without it, **confiscated or sunk**.
**Goa Inquisition (16th c.)** acted against religious dissent.
Telugu name for the Portuguese: **Budata Keechu**.

152.s:
Consider the following statements about Portuguese rule and decline:
1. A sustained increase in support from the Dutch and English was not a major factor in the decline of Portuguese power in India.
2. The term 'Cartaz' in the context of Portuguese rule in India refers to a naval trade licence or pass.
3. In the Telugu country the Portuguese were popularly called Budata Keechu.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
152.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Dutch and English competition, not support, contributed to Portuguese decline, along with weak successors, corruption and the 1580 merger with Spain.
Statement 2: Correct: a Cartaz was a Portuguese naval trade licence or pass required for ships in the Indian Ocean.
Statement 3: Correct: locals called the Portuguese Budata Keechu.

152.s:
Consider the following statements about Portuguese territorial losses:
1. Aurangzeb captured Hugli from the Portuguese in 1632.
2. The Portuguese lost Cochin to the Dutch in 1663.
3. Goa attained statehood in May 1961.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
152.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Shah Jahan, not Aurangzeb, took Hugli in 1632.
Statement 2: Correct: the Portuguese lost Cochin to the Dutch in 1663, after Pulicat (1610) and Nagapattinam (1658).
Statement 3: Incorrect: Goa became a state in May 1987; Portuguese rule had ended with Operation Vijay on 19 December 1961.

152.s:
Arrange the following Portuguese defeats by the English in chronological order:
A. Loss of Ormuz
B. Battle of Swally
C. Defeat off Jask
152.x: Swally (1612), off Jask (1620) and the loss of Ormuz (1622) to the English and the Shah of Persia.
xa: Losses to the **Dutch**: **Pulicat (1610)**, Nagapattinam, **Cochin (1663)**.
**Dutch and English competition** was an external cause of decline.
**Goa statehood:** **May 1987**.

152.s: Who were the first Europeans to set up sea trade centres in India?
152.x: Among all European powers in India, the Portuguese traders were the first to establish maritime trade centers in India. The first Portuguese Viceroy Francisco de Almeida annexed Diu in 1509 A.D. The victory of Diu made Portuguese most powerful in the Indian Ocean. During the battle of Diu in 1509 A.D. Portugese defeated the combined forces of Mamluk sultanate of Egypt, Gujarat sultanate (at western coast) and Zamorin of Calicut. The Portuguese established their monopoly over the Indian Ocean and levied a tax on ships passing through their area.

152.s: Which Fruit was introduced by the Portuguese to the Telugu soil?
152.x: The tomato, native to the Americas, was introduced to India by Portuguese traders as part of the Columbian Exchange, fundamentally transforming South Indian cooking and becoming integral to modern Telugu cuisine.

152.s: Hooghly was used as a base for piracy in the Bay of Bengal by :
152.x: The Portuguese used Hooghly as a base for piracy in the Bay of Bengal. In 1632 A.D., Qasim Khan who was the Governor of Bengal during Shahjahan’s reign finally subdued and imprisoned thousands of Portuguese.

153.s:
Consider the following statements about the Dutch East India Company:
1. The Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie (VOC) was formed on 20 March 1592.
2. The VOC received sovereign powers to wage war, build forts and sign treaties from the English Parliament.
3. Batavia was the headquarters of the VOC in Asia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
153.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the VOC was formed on 20 March 1602, not 1592.
Statement 2: Incorrect: these powers were granted by the Dutch States-General, not the English Parliament.
Statement 3: Correct: Batavia, now Jakarta, was the Asian headquarters of the VOC.

153.s:
Consider the following statements about the Dutch in India:
1. Cornelis de Houtman wrote the Itinerario, part of the background to Dutch expansion in Asia.
2. The Dutch were the first European traders in Andhra to obtain the right to collect land revenue.
3. Nagapattinam became the chief Dutch factory after the decline of Pulicat in 1690.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
153.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Linschoten wrote the Itinerario; Cornelis de Houtman reached Bantam in 1596.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the Dutch were the first to obtain the right to mint coins in Andhra, not to collect land revenue.
Statement 3: Correct: Pulicat was the chief Dutch centre until 1690, after which Nagapattinam became the chief factory.

153.s: Which of the following factories of Bengal was established by the Dutch?
153.x: & (c) The First Dutch Company in Bengal was set up in Pipali (1627 A.D.). About 1676 A.D. Dutches left the factory at Pipali and established new factory at Balasore. The trading in Bengal by Dutches was properly established in 1653 A.D., when they established their establishment in Chinsurah. Around 1656-57 A.D., Dutches properly established their own factory in Chinsurah. Also, Dutches established their factory in Hooghly, as the severe floods in 1600 A.D. in Hooghly trashed the factories established earlier. Hence, it is clear that, Dutches established their own factory at Chinsurah & Hooghly both. From the options, it’s clear that Dutch’s factories were established at Chinsurah (village in Hooghly) along with at Hooghly headquarter. Till the end of 17th century, Dutch companies were established at Qasim Bazar, Patna, Dhaka, Malda, Balasore, etc.

153.s:
Consider the following statements about the Dutch in Andhra:
1. The Dutch settled at Pulicat with the permission of the Zamorin of Calicut.
2. Van der Haghen set up the first Dutch factory in Andhra, at Machilipatnam, in 1605.
3. The Portuguese had traded at Machilipatnam before the establishment of the first Dutch factory there.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
153.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Pulicat was granted by the Chandragiri king, not the Zamorin of Calicut.
Statement 2: Correct: Van der Haghen set up the Machilipatnam factory in 1605 with permission from Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.
Statement 3: Correct: the Portuguese had traded at Machilipatnam before the Dutch established their factory there.

153.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
153.x: Nizampatnam was a Krishna delta weaving centre, not the Dutch headquarters. Pulicat was the headquarters until 1690.
153.tq: Reject the option that swaps a settlement's economic role with the headquarters.
xs: **Nizampatnam — HQ until 1690** is wrong; that was **Pulicat** — option **(3)**.
Nizampatnam (Petapoli) was a **Krishna delta weaving centre**.
**Draksharama** (trading post), **Bheemunipatnam** (**1641**) and **Palakollu** (Godavari weaving) are correct.
xa: HQ moved from Pulicat to **Nagapattinam** in **1690**.
Fort at Pulicat: **Fort Geldria**.
Other posts: **Jagannayakapuram**, **Gollapalem**, **Narasapur**, **Dronadam**.

153.s:
Consider the following statements about Dutch trade and decline:
1. The Dutch Andhra network extended broadly from Machilipatnam to Bheemunipatnam.
2. Silk and porcelain were imported into the Coromandel ports by the Dutch.
3. At the Battle of Colachel (1741), Travancore under Marthanda Varma defeated the French.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
153.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Dutch network in Andhra extended from Machilipatnam to Bheemunipatnam in the north-east.
Statement 2: Correct: silk and porcelain were imported, whereas gems, diamonds, indigo, cotton, Kalamkari and cloth were exported.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Travancore defeated the Dutch, not the French, at Colachel in 1741.

153.s:
Arrange the following Dutch factories in chronological order of establishment:
A. Surat
B. Chinsura
C. Karaikal
D. Nagapattinam
153.x: The correct sequence is Surat (1616), Karaikal (1645), Chinsura (1653) and Nagapattinam (1658).
153.tq: Place the earliest and latest years first, then resolve the middle pair.
xs: Order: **Surat (1616)**, **Karaikal (1645)**, **Chinsura (1653)**, **Nagapattinam (1658)** — **A, C, B, D**, option **(1)**.
Nagapattinam was **taken from the Portuguese**.
xa: **Cochin** followed in **1663**.
Other factories: **Kasimbazar**, **Baranagar**, **Balasore**, **Patna**, **Vengurla**.
**Chinsura** was the site of the **Bedara** battle (**1759**).

153.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
153.x: Pulicat was a hub of the slave trade to Batavia, not a centre of porcelain production. Koringa was associated with shipbuilding and Chittavalasa with jute.
153.tq: Find the option that substitutes a trade activity not associated with the stated port.
xs: **Pulicat — porcelain** is wrong: Pulicat was a hub of the **slave trade to Batavia** — option **(3)**.
**Porcelain** was an **import**, with silk.
**Koringa — shipbuilding** and **Chittavalasa — jute** are correct.
xa: Exports: gems, **diamonds**, **indigo**, cotton, **Kalamkari**, fine muslins.
Carrying trade: **saltpetre** (Bihar), opium, rice; pepper from Malabar.
**Koringa** factory: **1802**.

153.s: Which of the following pairs about the Battle of Bedara (Chinsura) is correctly matched?
o: Result – Dutch moved headquarters to Chinsura
153.x: At Bedara in 1759 the English under Francis Forde defeated the Dutch, who then withdrew to Indonesia.
xa: The Dutch side was led by **J.B. Russell**.
**Colachel (1741):** Travancore beat the Dutch.
**Chinsura** factory: **1653**.

153.s: Which statement regarding the Dutch establishment at Cochin is correct?
o: It was founded by the Dutch in 1605 and abandoned in 1690.
It was taken from Travancore in 1741 and returned to Portugal in 1824.
It was taken from the Portuguese in 1663 and passed to the British in 1795.
It was taken from the English in 1663 and ceded to the French in 1795.
153.x: The Dutch took Cochin from the Portuguese in 1663; it later passed to the British in 1795.
153.tq: Keep the predecessor, takeover year and later successor together as one sequence.
xs: The Dutch took **Cochin** from the **Portuguese** in **1663**; it passed to the **British (1795)** — option **(3)**.
**1605** is Machilipatnam; **1741** is Colachel; **1824** the Anglo-Dutch Treaty.
xa: **Pulicat** was ceded under the **Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824**.
Dutch occupation period: **1605-1825**.
Travancore's win at **Colachel (1741)** ended Dutch ambitions in **Malabar**.

153.s: Which of the following was a major reason for the decline of Dutch power in India?
o: Their Coromandel cloth trade was always more profitable than Indonesian spices.
They were supported by the English against all Indian powers.
They completely abandoned maritime trade after 1605.
Their priority was the Indonesian spice monopoly rather than Indian territorial expansion.
153.x: The Dutch prioritised their spice monopoly in Indonesia, while Malabar was less profitable to them than the Coromandel cloth trade. This weakened their long-term commitment to India.
153.tq: Choose the strategic explanation that links commercial priority with imperial decline.
xs: Their priority was the **Indonesian spice monopoly** — option **(4)**.
**Malabar** was less profitable than **Coromandel cloth** — but the spice monopoly came first, not cloth.
The English were **rivals**, not supporters (conferences of **1613** and **1615** failed).
xa: Defeats at **Colachel** and **Bedara**.
Lost **Andhra strongholds** in the Anglo-French wars.
Asian HQ: **Batavia**.

153.s: Pulicat was ceded by the Dutch under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of:
153.x: Pulicat was ceded under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824; the Dutch occupation is dated 1605-1825.
xa: At **Colachel** (**1741**) **Travancore** defeated the Dutch, ending Dutch ambitions in Malabar.
At **Bedara** (**1759**) the English (**Clive**, **Francis Forde**) defeated the Dutch (**J.B. Russell**).
The Dutch put their Indonesian spice monopoly first; Asian HQ was **Batavia**.

153.s: Mahe was a centre of the:
153.x: Mahe was a French centre; Kasimbazar, Balasore and Vengurla were Dutch.
xa: Other Dutch factories: **Baranagar**, **Patna**.
Elsewhere: **Surat (1616)**, **Karaikal (1645)**, **Chinsura (1653)**.
HQ: Pulicat till **1690**, then **Nagapattinam**.

153.s: In India, among the following locations, the Dutch established their earliest factory at
153.x: The Dutch East India Company established its first factory at Machilipatnam in 1605, followed by another at Petapuli in 1606. In 1609, the Dutch established a factory at Pulicat, near Chennai, which became the headquarters of their Coromandel Directorate in 1616. They later established trading depots at Nagapattinam, Kochi, Surat, Chinsurah, Agra, and Patna. In 1690, the Dutch shifted their headquarters from Pulicat to Nagapattinam on the southern Coromandel Coast.

153.s: At which place in Andhra did the Dutch East India Company set up its first factory?
153.x: The Dutch set up their first factory at Machilipatnam in 1605.

153.s: Where was the headquarters of the Dutch East India Company's settlements in India?
153.x: The Dutch moved their Coromandel headquarters from Pulicat to Nagapattinam in 1690.

153.s: In which of the following places the Dutch established their trading centre in India?
153.x: Important trading centers established by Dutch in India were- Nagappattinam. Chinsura, Machilipatnam, Surat, Pullicut, Agra, Kochin, Ahmedabad, Patna.

154.s:
Consider the following statements about the English East India Company:
1. The 1600 charter first gave the English East India Company a monopoly of East Indies trade for fifteen years.
2. The early English East India Company was run by a Governor and a 24-member committee, with shareholders forming the General Court.
3. Charles II and James II delegated to the Company powers of coining money, exercising jurisdiction and declaring war and peace with non-Christians.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
154.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the charter gave a fifteen-year monopoly, later made perpetual; it granted trading rights, not territorial power.
Statement 2: Correct: the Company was run by a Governor and a 24-member committee (later the Court of Directors); shareholders formed the General Court.
Statement 3: Correct: the delegated powers included coining money, jurisdiction and making war and peace with non-Christians.

154.s:
Consider the following statements about the English East India Company:
1. The English East India Company received its charter on 31 December 1600 from Charles II.
2. The English East India Company largely paid for Indian goods during its early trade with loans from the Mughal treasury.
3. The Farman of 1717, regarded as the "Magna Carta" of the Company's trade, was issued by Farrukhsiyar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
154.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Queen Elizabeth I, not Charles II, granted the charter on 31 December 1600.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the Company paid for Indian goods with imported bullion, not Mughal loans.
Statement 3: Correct: the Farman of 1717 was issued by Farrukhsiyar and substantially enhanced the Company's trading privileges.

154.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Ralph Fitch was the first English merchant to visit Akbar's court.
Ralph Fitch visited Agra and Fatehpur Sikri.
154.x: Option C is incorrect: Ralph Fitch was in India from 1583 to 1586, not 1586 to 1589. He visited Agra and Fatehpur Sikri and was the first English merchant at Akbar's court.
154.tq: Recall the dates of Ralph Fitch's visit.
n: Ralph Fitch visited India during 1583–1586. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 35-40]
Ralph Fitch visited Agra. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 35-40]
Ralph Fitch visited Fatehpur Sikri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 35-40]
Ralph Fitch was the first English merchant to visit Akbar's court. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 35-40]
xs: The incorrect statement: Ralph Fitch visited India during **1586–1589** — option **(3)**.
**Ralph Fitch** visited India **1583–1586**.
He visited **Agra** and **Fatehpur Sikri** and was the **first English merchant** at **Akbar's court**.
xa: **Akbar** (**1556 to 1605**) was contemporary with **Queen Elizabeth I** (**1558 to 1603**).
The EIC was formed in **1600**, during Akbar's reign.
The EIC's first voyage was in **1602** under **James Lancaster**, to **Bantam**.

154.s:
Consider the following statements about the English East India Company:
1. The English East India Company was formed in 1600 during the reign of the Mughal emperor Akbar.
2. The English East India Company was established in 1764.
3. Visakhapatnam became the first municipality in Andhra, in 1861.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
154.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the charter came from Elizabeth I on 31 December 1600, during Akbar's reign (1556-1605).
Statement 2: Incorrect: the Company was established in 1600; 1764 is the Battle of Buxar.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Bhimili, not Visakhapatnam, became Andhra's first municipality in 1861.

154.s:
Consider the following statements about English factories and presidencies:
1. The English ship Globe reached Machilipatnam in 1611 under the command of Sir Thomas Roe.
2. Bombay was leased to the English East India Company in 1668 by Charles II.
3. Madras, including Fort St. George, was founded in 1639 by Francis Day after obtaining a grant from Venkatapati Raya III.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
154.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the Globe reached Machilipatnam in 1611 under Captain Anthony Hippon, not Sir Thomas Roe.
Statement 2: Correct: Charles II leased Bombay to the Company in 1668.
Statement 3: Correct: Francis Day founded Madras in 1639 with a grant from the Chandragiri ruler Venkatapati Raya III, helped by the Damerla brothers.

154.s:
Consider the following statements about English presidencies:
1. The Madras Presidency had its seat at Fort St. George.
2. Bombay was handed over to the East India Company by the English Crown in 1668 for an annual rent of £10.
3. The zamindari of Sutanuti, Gobindapur and Kalikata, which formed the basis of Calcutta, was acquired by the Company in 1698.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
154.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Madras was at Fort St. George and Calcutta at Fort William in Bengal.
Statement 2: Correct: in 1668 Bombay was transferred to the Company for an annual rent of £10.
Statement 3: Correct: in 1698 the Company bought the zamindari rights of Sutanuti, Gobindapur and Kalikata.

154.s:
Consider the following statements about early English factories:
1. The first permanent English factory in India was set up in 1613 at Hooghly.
2. Sutanuti, one of the three villages that became Calcutta, was an English trading centre.
3. Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese in the Battle of Swally (1612).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
154.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the first permanent English factory was at Surat in 1613, not Hooghly.
Statement 2: Correct: Sutanuti was an English trading centre and a Calcutta base.
Statement 3: Correct: Captain Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese at Swally near Surat in 1612.

154.s: Which of the following pairs (factory – year) is correctly matched?
154.x: The Dutch set up at Surat in 1616; the English were at Masulipatnam in 1611 and Surat in 1613, and the French at Surat in 1668.
n: Surat was associated with English European trade in 1613. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 64-67]
The Dutch established a factory at Surat in 1616. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 64-67]
The French established a factory at Surat in 1668. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 64-67]
The English East India Company established a factory at Masulipatnam in 1611. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 64-67]
The English East India Company established a factory at Masulipatnam in 1611. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 64-67]
The English East India Company established a factory at Surat in 1613. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 64-67]
The Dutch established a factory at Surat in 1616. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 64-67]
The French established a factory at Surat in 1668. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 64-67]
Surat had an English East India Company factory in 1613. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 64-67]
xa: Masulipatnam = **first temporary** English factory; Surat = **first permanent**.
**Madras (Fort St. George)** followed in **1639**.
**Bombay** was leased from **Charles II** in **1668**.

154.s:
Arrange the following English settlements on the Andhra coast in chronological order:
A. Armagaon
B. Visakhapatnam
C. Machilipatnam
D. Pulicat
154.x: The settlements were established at Machilipatnam in 1611, Pulicat in 1621, Armagaon in 1626 and Visakhapatnam in 1682.
154.tq: Fix the first and last events, then arrange the middle dates.
xs: Order: **Machilipatnam (1611)**, **Pulicat (1621)**, **Armagaon (1626)**, **Visakhapatnam (1682)** — **C, D, A, B**, option **(1)**.
Pulicat was **abandoned** due to Dutch hostility.
xa: After Armagaon, back to Machilipatnam, then **Madras (1639)**.
Other factories: **Nizampatnam**, **Narsapuram**, **Veeravasaram**, **Bheemunipatnam**.
**Bhimili** = first municipality in Andhra (**1861**).

154.s: Which one of the following statements about Armagaon is correct?
o: It was established in 1611 at Machilipatnam by Captain Anthony Hippon.
It was established in 1639 at Madras by Francis Day.
It was established in 1626 at Dugarajapatnam and was named after Karanam Armugam Mudali.
It was established in 1682 at Visakhapatnam by Job Charnock.
154.x: Armagaon was established in 1626 at Dugarajapatnam, now in Tirupati district, and was named after Karanam Armugam Mudali.
154.tq: Combine place, date and names to defeat swapped-founder options.
xs: **Armagaon (1626)**, at **Dugarajapatnam**, was named after **Karanam Armugam Mudali** — option **(3)**.
**1611** is Machilipatnam (Hippon); **1639** Madras (Francis Day); **1682** Visakhapatnam.
xa: Armagaon was the **3rd** Andhra settlement, now in **Tirupati district**.
It lay **35 miles north of Pulicat**.
Job Charnock founded Calcutta, not any Andhra post.

154.s:
Consider the following statements about the East India Company's growth:
1. Under Farrukhsiyar's Farman of 1717, the Company's Bengal trade became duty-free for an annual payment of Rs 3,000.
2. Bengal became the first major territorial base of the East India Company.
3. The early objective of the East India Company was eastern trade, especially in spices and textiles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
154.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Bengal trade became duty-free for Rs 3,000 a year with the right to issue dastaks.
Statement 2: Correct: Bengal became the Company's first major territorial base after Plassey (1757) and the grant of Diwani (1765).
Statement 3: Correct: the Company's early objective was eastern trade, especially in spices and textiles.

154.s:
Consider the following statements about the Company's rise in Bengal:
1. The mission that secured the Farman of 1717 from Farrukhsiyar was led by William Hawkins.
2. The misuse of dastaks by the East India Company drained the Nawab's revenue through private trade.
3. The Battle of Buxar was fought in 1764.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
154.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the mission to Farrukhsiyar's court was led by John Surman, not William Hawkins.
Statement 2: Correct: Company servants misused dastaks for private trade, depriving the Nawab of Bengal of revenue.
Statement 3: Correct: Buxar was fought in 1764, after Plassey (1757).

154.s:
Consider the following statements about English East India Company milestones:
1. Child's War (1686–1690) was fought between the English East India Company and Jahangir.
2. The Golden Farman issued by the Sultan of Golconda granted the English free trade in Golconda ports on payment of 500 pagodas annually.
3. Madras became the first municipality in India in 1687.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
154.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Child's War was fought against Aurangzeb, not Jahangir.
Statement 2: Correct: the Golden Farman permitted free trade in Golconda ports for an annual payment of 500 pagodas.
Statement 3: Correct: Madras was India's first municipality in 1687; Bhimili was Andhra's first in 1861.

154.s: Shivaji’s attacks on Surat had which effect on the English East India Company?
o: He transferred the Surat factory to Madras.
He twice sacked Surat and threatened the English factory there.
He helped the English defeat the Portuguese at Swally.
He granted the English a monopoly over Surat trade.
154.x: Shivaji sacked Surat twice and threatened the English factory located there.
154.tq: Apply the consequence of a regional military event to the Company’s settlement.
xs: **Shivaji** **sacked Surat twice** and threatened the English factory — option **(2)**.
**Swally (1612)** was Thomas Best's victory, not Shivaji's.
xa: **Bombay** replaced **Surat** as the chief west-coast settlement.
Bombay came to the Company in **1668** for **£10 a year**.
Surat factory followed **Jahangir's farman (1613)**.

154.s: Permission for the English to establish their first factory at Machilipatnam in 1611 was granted by:
154.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah permitted the English to establish their first factory at Machilipatnam in 1611.
154.tq: Use the founder-or-grantor trap in a regional history question.
xs: **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** gave permission — option **(3)**; he ruled **1580-1612**, so it fits **1611**.
⚠ APPSC G2 **2008** key named **Ibrahim Qutb Shah** — but Ibrahim died in **1580**.
**Abdullah Qutb Shah** issued the **Golden Farman** later.
xa: **Captain Anthony Hippon** came in the ship **"Globe"**.
First English factory: **Surat** (India), **Machilipatnam** (Andhra).
Next Andhra moves: **Pulicat (1621)**, **Armagaon (1626)**.

154.s: In which year was the English East India Company established?
154.x: The English East India Company was chartered by Queen Elizabeth I on 31 December 1600, gaining a monopoly over English trade with the East Indies. This marked the formal start of England's commercial and eventually colonial engagement with India. From there the arc runs through Surat, Madras, Bombay and Calcutta to political dominance after Plassey (1757) and Buxar (1764).

154.s: First Englishman who visited Akbar’s court was –
154.x: Ralph Fitch (1583-86 A.D.) was the English merchant who visited Agra and Fatehpur Sikri. He observed various places of India by travelling and presented precious narrative about Indian trade points and township centres of the 16th century.

154.s: Which one of the following was the Emperor of India when the British East India Company was formed in London?
154.x: Plans were prepared by some merchants for trading with eastern islands, so East India Company for the fulfilment of this purpose was founded in 1600 A.D. by the Royal Charter of Queen Elizabeth I and it was named as The Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies. At that time, Akbar was the Emperor of India (1556- 1605 A.D.).

154.s: Who was the ruler of India when the English East India Company was formed?
154.x: English East India Company was formed in the year 1600 A.D.. Elizabeth was the queen of England and Akbar was the emperor of India at that time.

154.s: The secret of success of East India Company in India was :
o: The company army received western training and they
Indian Soldiers lacked fidelity consequently the one
154.x: All the three factors were helpful in the success of East India Company in India. It is known that a group called Merchants Adventures in England formed East India company or ‘The Governor and company of Merchants of London trading into the East Indies.’ In December 1600, Queen Elizabeth I of England granted a royal charter to do business with the East Indies.

154.s: Which of the following British companies got the first charter permitting them to trade in India?
o: The English Company trading to the East Indies
154.x: The Levant Company (1592) was granted a monopoly to trade with Ottoman Empire (The Levant) and its eastern areas (including India). They traded in Silk, spices etc. After the ‘Royal Charter’ of Queen Elizabeth I, the East India Company was provided with exclusive 15-year monopoly on English trade with all countries east of Cape of Good Hope, which included India.
