The partition of Bengal finally took place on 16th October, 1905 A.D. On 7 August, 1905 A.D., one of the first mass protests was organized in Calcutta’s Town Hall, also known as Anti-partition Movement. 3. When did the Anti-Partition Movement begin with a massive demonstration at the Town Hall, Calcutta? (a) 16th October, 1905 (b) 7th August, 1905 (c) 16th August, 1905 (d) 5th August, 1905 U.P. R.O/A.R.O (Re. Exam) (Pre) 2025 Ans. (b)

167.s: Who among the following negotiated Subordinate Alliances of 1817-18 with the Princely States of Rajputana?
167.x: Lord Hastings sought to impose British Paramountcy in India for which suppression of the Marathas and the Pindaris was essential. He looked upon the Rajputana states as his natural allies against the Marathas and the Pindaris. Charles Metcalf was entrusted with the duty of negotiating alliances with princely states of Rajputana.

167.s:
Consider the following Indian states:
I. Awadh
II. Jhansi
III. Satara
IV. Nagpur
V. Sindh
Which of the above states were annexed by the British due to the policy of Doctrine of Lapse?
167.x: The Doctrine of Lapse was introduced by Lord Dalhousie. Under this policy, princely states without a natural male heir were annexed by the British. States annexed through this doctrine included Jhansi, Satara, and Nagpur.

167.s:
Consider the following Princely States of the British rule in India:
1. Jhansi
2. Sambalpur
3. Satara The correct chronological order in which they were annexed by the British is:
167.x: The annexations took place under the policy of the Doctrine of Lapse introduced by Lord Dalhousie. Satara was annexed first in 1848, followed by Sambalpur in 1849, and Jhansi in 1854.

167.s: Which was the first State to be merged under Dalhousie's "Doctrine of Lapse"?
167.x: The doctrine of lapse was the policy of Lord Dalhousie to annex the independent Indian State on the certain ground i.e. if Ruler of State died childless or was manifestly incompetent. The doctrine of lapse first applied to the State of Satara in 1848 A.D.

167.s: Awadh was annexed to British Empire in India by :
o: By declaring the State as maladministered
167.x: Lord Dalhousie efficiently made the plan and accused Nawab of Awadh, Wajid Ali Shah for maladministration and merged his state into the British Empire in February 1856. He sent his officer to inquire about the ground reality who sent him a detailed report regarding maladministration. He sent that report to London to obtain permission to merge the Awadh. Lord Dalhousie (1848-56) merged Satara in 1848, Jaitpur and Sambalpur in 1849, Baghat in 1850, Udaipur in 1852, Jhansi in 1854 and Nagpur in 1854 under the principle of Doctrine of Lapse.

167.s: Which of the following was the first victim of Lord Dalhousie’s ‘policy of doctrine of lapse’?
167.x: The doctrine of lapse was the policy of Lord Dalhousie to annex the independent Indian State on the certain ground i.e. if Ruler of State died childless or was manifestly incompetent. The doctrine of lapse first applied to the State of Satara in 1848 A.D.

167.s:
Consider the following Princely States of the British rule in India :
1. Jhansi
2. Sambalpur
3. Satara The correct chronological order in which they were annexed by the British is :
167.x: Satara was annexed by Dalhousie in 1848 A.D., Sambalpur in Orissa was annexed by him in 1849 A.D. Jhansi was annexed in 1854 A.D. All these states were annexed by Dalhousie on the principle of “Doctrine of Lapse.”

167.s: Which among the following was not one of those states which were annexed to the British Empire by Lord Dalhousie on the pretext of the ‘Doctrine of Lapse’?
167.x: 51. Which of the following State was not annexed under Lord Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse? (a) Nagpur (b) Jaipur (c) Sambhalpur (d) Satara 70th B.P.S.C. Re-Exam 2024 Ans. (b) Lord Dalhousie (1848-56 A.D.) accused the Nawab of Awadh, Wajid Ali Shah, of misgovernance and annexed Awadh into British territory in February 1856 A.D.. Besides Awadh, Dalhousie implemented the Doctrine of Lapse to annex the following territories: - Satara (1848 A.D.) - Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849 A.D.) - Bhagat (1850 A.D.) - Udaipur (1852 A.D.) - Jhansi (1853 A.D. ) - Nagpur (1854 A.D.)

167.s: Oudh was amalgamated into the British dominion in the year–
167.x: Sind was annexed during the tenure of Lord Ellenborough (1842-1844 AD). Awadh was annexed in 1856 AD on the ground of maladministration during Lord Dalhousie tenure. Satara was annexed in 1848 AD.

167.s:
Consider the annexation of the following States under 'Doctrine of Lapse' and arrange them into chronological order :
1. Satara
2. Jhansi
3. Baghat
4. Udaipur
Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
167.x: Sind was annexed during the tenure of Lord Ellenborough (1842-1844 AD). Awadh was annexed in 1856 AD on the ground of maladministration during Lord Dalhousie tenure. Satara was annexed in 1848 AD.

167.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
167.x: Lower Burma, also called Pegu, was annexed by conquest in 1852. Berar was taken from the Nizam for arrears, Awadh for misgovernment, and Sindh by conquest in 1843.
167.tq: Check both the ground and the year instead of accepting a familiar territory name.
xs: **Lower Burma (Pegu)** was annexed by **conquest** in **1852** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Berar (1853)** was taken from the Nizam for **arrears**, not misgovernment.
**Awadh** was annexed in **1856** for **misgovernment**, not conquest in 1843.
**Sindh** was annexed by **conquest** under **Ellenborough** in **1843**, not by lapse in 1848.
xa: **Satara (1848)** was the first lapse annexation.
**Punjab (1849)** was also a conquest, after the **Second Anglo-Sikh War**; **Duleep Singh** was deposed.

167.s: How did the British get Rayalaseema from the Nizam?
167.x: Under the Subsidiary Alliance treaty of 12 October 1800 the Nizam ceded Rayalaseema (Ceded Districts) to the British.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about the Northern Circars:
1. Nellore was one of the five traditional Circars of the Northern Circars.
2. The annual payment obtained through Kandregula Jogipantulu's negotiations for the lease of the Circars was 15 lakh rupees.
3. Kandregula Jogipantulu is known as a dubashi and envoy between the Nizam's court and the Company.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
168.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the five Circars were Chicacole, Rajahmundry, Ellore, Mustafanagar and Guntur; Nellore was not one of them.
Statement 2: Correct: Jogipantulu used the Gollapudi mutiny to get the Circars leased to the Company for 15 lakh rupees a year (1766).
Statement 3: Correct: Jogipantulu was a prominent dubashi and envoy between the Nizam's court and the Company's men at Machilipatnam.

168.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
168.x: The Treaty of Masulipatnam was 1768; Salabat Jung's grant was 1759, the Circar lease 1766 and the Treaty of Hyderabad 1798.
xa: **1788**: **Guntur** handed over for **7 lakh**.
**1800**: **Ceded Districts** given in lieu of the subsidy.
**1801**: Nellore and Chittoor annexed; Andhra merged into the **Madras Presidency**.

168.s: Under the Treaty of Masulipatnam of 1768, which arrangement was made?
o: The Nizam handed over Guntur after receiving 7 lakh rupees.
The Company leased the Circars for an annual payment of 15 lakh rupees.
The Nizam ceded all the Ceded Districts in lieu of the subsidiary subsidy.
The Company retained the Circars for a reduced peshkash of 9 lakh rupees annually and provided military help to the Nizam.
168.x: The Treaty of Masulipatnam allowed the Company to retain the Circars for a reduced annual peshkash of 9 lakh rupees, along with military assistance to the Nizam.
168.tq: Separate the terms of the 1768 treaty from the earlier lease and later cession.
xs: By the **Treaty of Masulipatnam (1768)** the Company **retained the Circars for a reduced peshkash of 9 lakh** a year plus **military help** to the Nizam — option **(4)**.
**15 lakh** was the **1766** lease; **7 lakh** was the **Guntur** payment of **1788**; the **Ceded Districts** came in **1800**.
xa: The 1768 treaty settled the dispute over the Mughal firman of **1765**.
**Guntur** was excepted from the Circar lease until **1788**.
⚠ **15 lakh** = 1766 lease; **9 lakh** = 1768; **7 lakh** = Guntur.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about the Northern Circars and Bobbili:
1. In the Bobbili War (1757), Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram took the help of the French under Bussy.
2. Kolis, Bhils and Todas formed the hereditary zamindari families of the Northern Circars.
3. In the aftermath of the Battle of Bobbili (1757), Tandra Papayya killed Vijayaramaraju of Vizianagaram.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
168.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Vijayarama Raju took French help through Bussy in the Bobbili War of 1757.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the hereditary zamindari families included Velamas, Reddis and Kshatriya Rajus.
Statement 3: Correct: Tandra Papayya, brother-in-law of Bobbili Ranga Rao, killed Vijayaramaraju to avenge Bobbili.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about land revenue in Andhra:
1. The Nizam ceded the 'Ceded Districts' to the British in 1800.
2. Over-assessment, indebtedness to moneylenders and land alienation were major consequences of the Ryotwari system in the Andhra region.
3. Zamindari prevailed in the Northern Circars and Ryotwari in Rayalaseema, later extending to most of Andhra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
168.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Nizam ceded them in 1800 because he could not pay the Subsidiary Alliance subsidy in cash.
Statement 2: Correct: Ryotwari areas saw assessment often above 50 percent of the produce, dependence on moneylenders and land alienation.
Statement 3: Correct: Zamindari prevailed in the Northern Circars, while Ryotwari was associated with Rayalaseema and later covered most of Andhra.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about Company rule in Andhra:
1. The Permanent Settlement, introduced by Cornwallis in 1793, was applied to the Andhra zamindaris in 1802.
2. The Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam was concluded in 1798.
3. The Battle of Padmanabham was fought in 1802.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
168.x:
Statement 1: Correct: it was applied in Andhra in 1802, replacing the auction of zamindaris with a fixed demand.
Statement 2: Correct: the Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam came in 1798.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the Battle of Padmanabham was fought in 1794, not 1802.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra under British rule:
1. Zamindari was abolished in the Madras Presidency in 1956.
2. During the early administration of the Northern Circars, collectors relied on dubashis as intermediaries.
3. Dharmavaram and Madanapalle are present-day silk hubs of Rayalaseema.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
168.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Zamindari in Madras was abolished in 1948, not 1956.
Statement 2: Correct: Collectors relied on dubashis for administrative and local assistance.
Statement 3: Correct: Dharmavaram and Madanapalle are present-day silk hubs; the British promoted sericulture in the Ceded Districts.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra under the Company:
1. Nellore-Chittoor came under Company rule last, after the Circars, Guntur and the Ceded Districts.
2. The divergence between the fertile, educated Circars and the arid, neglected Ceded Districts later influenced debates surrounding the Sri Bagh Pact.
3. After the Second Carnatic War, the British installed Muhammad Ali as the Nawab of the Carnatic.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
168.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Circars came in 1766, Guntur in 1788, the Ceded Districts in 1800 and Nellore-Chittoor in 1801.
Statement 2: Correct: the contrasting development of the Circars and the Ceded Districts later shaped the Sri Bagh Pact debate.
Statement 3: Correct: the British installed Muhammad Ali, though his position became secure only after 1763.

168.s:
Assertion (A): In 1794 the Chief-and-Council system in the Northern Circars was replaced by District Collectors.
Reason (R): The Permanent Settlement was introduced in the Northern Circars in 1802.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
168.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Collectors replaced the Chiefs and Councils in 1794, while the Permanent Settlement came later, in 1802, so it cannot explain the earlier change.
168.tq: Check the dates: a later reform cannot explain an earlier one.
n: The Collector’s administration came into existence in place of the Board of Revenue in 1794. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 15-16]
The Office of Collector was introduced in the North Sarkar region in 1802. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 15-16]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.
A: in **1794** the **Chiefs and Councils** were replaced by **District Collectors**.
R: the **Permanent Settlement** reached Andhra in **1802** — later, so it cannot explain A.
xa: ⚠ Exam key: "Collector's administration in place of the Revenue Board" = **1786** (APPSC G2 **2012**).
From **1794** each Collector handled land revenue, law and order and magistracy; judicial powers removed in **1816**.
The **Office of Collector** reached the **North Sarkar region** in **1802**.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about the Circars and Ceded Districts:
1. Robert Clive secured the firman relating to the Mughal grant of the Northern Circars from Shah Alam II.
2. The Ceded Districts in 1800 comprised Kadapa, Chittoor, Nellore and Kurnool.
3. The name 'Rayalaseema' for the Ceded Districts was suggested by C.P. Brown.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
168.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Clive secured the firman from Shah Alam II; it is dated 1765.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the Ceded Districts comprised Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the name was suggested by Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao; C.P. Brown was a Telugu scholar.

168.s: The first Telugu to English dictionary was composed by
168.x: Charles Philip Brown, a 19th-century British civil servant and Telugu scholar, compiled one of the earliest authoritative Telugu-English dictionaries and edited classical texts such as Vemana's. His work was foundational to modern Telugu lexicography. Sir Thomas Munro, linked to the Ryotwari system, is the common distractor.

168.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
168.x: Read and Munro conducted the Baramahal experiment in 1792; Munro's Ceded Districts experiment dates to 1802.
xa: Munro brought **Ryotwari** from the **Bara Mahals** to the Ceded Districts.
Ryotwari extended across **Madras** in **1820** under Governor Munro.
Munro surveyed the Ceded Districts **1802-07**.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about Company-era figures in Andhra:
1. Thomas Munro became the first Collector of the Ceded Districts in 1800.
2. C.P. Brown is associated with the publication of Vemana's verses and a Telugu-English dictionary.
3. V. Veeranna was the Andhra officer who helped Sir Arthur Cotton build the Godavari barrage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
168.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Thomas Munro became the first Collector of the Ceded Districts in 1800.
Statement 2: Correct: C.P. Brown published Vemana's verses and a Telugu-English dictionary.
Statement 3: Correct: Veneti (Veenam) Veeranna helped Cotton build the Godavari barrage.

168.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Thomas Munro — Introduced Ryotwari and surveyed the districts from 1802 to 1807
C.P. Brown — Built the Dowleswaram anicut
George Russell — Governor of Madras from 1820 to 1827
168.x: Munro introduced Ryotwari and surveyed the Ceded Districts during 1802–07. Arthur Cotton was the irrigation engineer, C.P. Brown was the Telugu scholar, and Munro—not George Russell—was Governor of Madras from 1820 to 1827.
xs: **Munro** introduced **Ryotwari** and surveyed the districts **1802-07** — option **(1)**.
**Cotton** built the **Dowleswaram anicut**; **Brown** published **Vemana**'s verses; **Munro**, not Russell, was Governor of Madras **1820-27**.
xa: **George Russell** took charge of the Vizianagaram forts after Padmanabham.
⚠ **Cotton**'s assistant = **Veenam Veeranna**; **Brown** = Vemana.

168.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Veenam Veeranna — Andhra assistant to Arthur Cotton
168.x: The Dowleswaram anicut was built across the Godavari. Arthur Cotton built the Krishna anicut at Vijayawada, and Veenam Veeranna served as his Andhra assistant.
xs: **Dowleswaram anicut — Krishna** is wrong: Dowleswaram is on the **Godavari** — option **(1)**.
The others are correct: **Veenam Veeranna** was Cotton's Andhra assistant; the **Krishna anicut** is at **Vijayawada**.
xa: **Sir Arthur Cotton** built both anicuts.
**Veenam Veeranna** = **APPSC G2 2019** key.

168.s: Which of the following statements about Thomas Munro in the Andhra region is correct?
o: He introduced mahalwari settlement from Punjab into the Ceded Districts and died at Hyderabad in 1827.
He introduced permanent settlement from Bengal into the Circars and died at Madras in 1801.
He introduced zamindari in Rayalaseema and died at Nellore in 1816.
He introduced ryotwari from the Bara Mahals into the Ceded Districts and died at Pattikonda as Governor in 1827.
168.x: Munro brought the ryotwari system from the Bara Mahals to the Ceded Districts. He died at Pattikonda in Kurnool district in 1827 while serving as Governor.
168.tq: Combine the reformer's policy, source region, destination and death details without swapping settlement systems.
xs: **Munro** brought **Ryotwari** from the **Bara Mahals** to the Ceded Districts and died as Governor at **Pattikonda** in **1827** — option **(4)**.
The **Permanent Settlement** was Cornwallis's, not Munro's; Munro died at Pattikonda (**Kurnool**), not Hyderabad.
xa: In Baramahal (**1792**) he worked with **Captain Alexander Read**.
Date of death: **6 July 1827**; Governor of Madras **1820-27**.

168.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its historical description?
168.x: Vizianagaram was associated with the Pusapati family. Bobbili and Venkatagiri were associated with Velama families, while Peddapuram belonged to the Vatsavayi dynasty.
168.tq: Separate similar zamindari houses through family-name associations.
xs: **Vizianagaram — Pusapati** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Bobbili** was a **Velama** estate; **Venkatagiri** = **Velugoti**; **Peddapuram** = **Vatsavayi**.
xa: Bobbili was destroyed in the **1757** war by Vizianagaram and the French.
Venkatagiri was a Velama zamindari in **Nellore**.
⚠ **Pusapati** = Vizianagaram; **Velugoti** = Venkatagiri; **Vatsavayi** = Peddapuram.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about Zamindari in the Northern Circars:
1. After Chinna Vijayarama Raju's defeat at Padmanabham (1794), George Russell was placed over Vizianagaram's forts.
2. Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram were estates under the Zamindari system.
3. An important effect of the Zamindari system in the Northern Circars was absentee landlordism and impoverishment of tenants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
168.x:
Statement 1: Correct: after the defeat, Narayana Babu was made zamindar and George Russell was put in charge of Vizianagaram's forts.
Statement 2: Correct: Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram were Zamindari estates.
Statement 3: Correct: the Zamindari system encouraged absentee landlordism and impoverished tenants.

168.s: Which of the following statements regarding the zamindaris of the Northern Circars is correct?
o: The Permanent Settlement abolished fixed revenue for zamindars.
The Northern Circars had no hereditary zamindari families.
Only Venkatagiri was brought under the Permanent Settlement.
Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram were pre-existing estates brought under the Permanent Settlement.
168.x: Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram were pre-existing estates brought under the Permanent Settlement. The settlement made zamindars fixed-revenue holders.
168.tq: Reject the absolute statement and identify the precise estate group.
xs: **Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram** were **pre-existing estates** brought under the **Permanent Settlement** — option **(4)**.
The settlement made zamindars **fixed-revenue** holders — it did not abolish fixed revenue.
The Circars did have hereditary families — **Velamas, Reddis, Kshatriya Rajus**.
xa: **Permanent Settlement**: **Cornwallis**, **1793**; applied in Andhra in **1802**.
Effect: **absentee landlordism**; tenants impoverished.
Zamindari abolished by the **Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948**, in force **7 Sep 1949**.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about Company administration in Madras:
1. Under Company revenue administration, the officer at the taluk level was the Tahsildar.
2. The post of District Judge, under whom the Zilla or District Court functioned, was created by the Madras District Police Act of 1859.
3. British judicial procedure that replaced village panchayats was criticised mainly because it was slow and costly and contributed to litigation and debt.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
168.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Tahsildar was at the taluk level, below the Collector at district level.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the post of District Judge was created under the Cornwallis Code of 1793.
Statement 3: Correct: British judicial procedure was criticised as slow and costly, increasing litigation and indebtedness.

168.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the judicial hierarchy in the Madras Presidency?
168.x: The Munsiff Court functioned at the taluk level, while the Zilla Court functioned at the district level. Sadar Adalats were apex courts for natives at Madras.
168.tq: Use the administrative level as the anchor for matching the court.
xs: **Taluk — Munsiff Court** is correct — option **(3)**.
The **Zilla Court** was at the **district** level; **Sadar Adalat** was the apex civil court at Madras.
xa: Appeal: **Provincial Courts of Appeal / Circuit courts** (powers expanded in **1820**).
Apex criminal court: **Sadar Faujdari Adalat**.
**Madras Supreme Court (1801)** for British subjects in Madras town.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about Company-era revenue terms:
1. 'Peshkash' refers to the share of revenue paid by zamindars to the British.
2. Haveli lands in coastal Andhra were lands held directly under British control.
3. Under Company rule, 'Sayer' referred to inland transit and customs duties on goods.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
168.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Peshkash was the share of revenue paid by zamindars to the British.
Statement 2: Correct: Haveli lands were under direct British control in coastal Andhra.
Statement 3: Correct: Sayer was the inland transit and customs duty.

168.s: Moturpha was levied mainly on which of the following?
o: Trades and occupations such as looms, shops and artisan activities
168.x: Moturpha was imposed on trades and occupations, including looms, shops and artisans. It was not a salt tax.
168.tq: Separate the look-alike revenue terms by identifying the actual taxable activity.
xs: **Moturpha** was a tax on **trades and occupations — looms, shops, artisans** — option **(1)**.
It was **not a salt tax**; liquor and toddy fell under **Abkari**, and zamindars' land revenue was **Peshkash**.
xa: **APPSC G2 2011** key: Moturpha = **tax on looms**.
The **Madras Native Association's 1861** petition complained about it.
**Sayer** = inland transit and customs duties.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about Company-era legal reforms:
1. The Indian Penal Code was enacted in 1860.
2. Thomas Munro was President of the Judicial Commission constituted in 1814.
3. The Madras Regulations of 1816 provided for the abolition of all village-level judicial institutions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
168.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the IPC dates to 1860.
Statement 2: Correct: Munro presided over the Judicial Commission of 1814, whose report came in April 1816.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the 1816 Regulations established Munsiff and Panchayat courts as courts of first instance.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about police and judicial administration:
1. The District Judge created thanas under the supervision of darogas in the early British police administration.
2. Munro's police reforms of 1816 transferred police supervision from judges to Collectors.
3. A Supreme Court plea seeking a separate revenue judicial service cadre, since revenue officers lack legal training to decide land-title disputes, invoked Article 14.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
168.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Lord Cornwallis created thanas under darogas.
Statement 2: Correct: Munro's 1816 changes transferred police supervision from judges to Collectors.
Statement 3: Correct: the plea invoked Article 14, and the Supreme Court issued notice on it.

168.s: The term 'Moturpha' is related to?
168.x: Moturpha was a tax on trades and professions, including looms, in the Madras Presidency.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about Company administration in Andhra:
1. The Circuit Committee recommended continuation of the auction system of revenue collection with higher minimum bids.
2. In the Madras Presidency, the Collector's administration was introduced in place of the Revenue Board in 1786.
3. Chittoor district was carved out, giving Kadapa its present area, in 1858.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
168.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the Circuit Committee recommended abolishing the auction system, which Munro then abolished in Rayalaseema.
Statement 2: Correct: the APPSC Group 2 (2012) key gives 1786.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Chittoor was carved out in 1911; 1858 is when Kurnool district was created.

168.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
168.x: West Godavari was created in 1925, not 1911. Kurnool, Anantapur, and Guntur with East Godavari were associated with 1858, 1882, and 1904 respectively.
168.tq: Find the one incorrect district-formation year.
xs: **West Godavari — 1911** is wrong: it was formed in **1925** — option **(4)**.
Correct: **Guntur and East Godavari — 1904**, **Kurnool — 1858**, **Anantapur — 1882**.
xa: **1911** = **Chittoor** carved out, giving **Kadapa** its present area.
Coastal Andhra had **5 districts**: **Ganjam, Visakhapatnam, Godavari, Krishna, Nellore**.
⚠ Exam angle: the **Kadapa 1911** trap.

168.s: The first Indian ruler to accept Lord Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance was:
168.x: The Nizam of Hyderabad accepted the Subsidiary Alliance first, by the Treaty of Hyderabad in 1798, and kept a British subsidiary force at his own cost. Baji Rao II accepted it later, in 1802, by the Treaty of Bassein. Tipu Sultan refused it. The Nawab of Awadh accepted it after the Nizam.
xs: The **Nizam of Hyderabad** was the first ruler to accept **Wellesley's** Subsidiary Alliance (**1798**) — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2002**).
Under the **Treaty of Hyderabad (1798)** the Nizam kept a British subsidiary force and paid for it.
xa: In **1800** he gave up the **Ceded Districts** in lieu of the subsidy.
Earlier treaties with the Nizam: **1766** lease, **1768** Masulipatnam, **1788** Guntur.

This system was launched in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Varanasi (U.P.) etc. It is also known as Istimarari Maalguzari, Bishwedari etc. The Permanent Settlement stood on the following features - It recognized the landlords as the proprietors of the land. All their rights ended if they failed to pay. This was one reason for increased litigation. An increase in intermediaries between farmers and landlords was another reason for increased litigation. 171.s: Who declared 'Sati' illegal?
171.x: The meaning of Sati is ‘holy and virtuous woman.’ In Hindu rituals, the marriage is considered as Sanskar which means ‘relation of spirits.’ The Brahmins of the 18th century used to believe that if a woman became Sati, seven generations of his husband will achieve heaven. It was quite famous among highly reputed Brahmins, Kshatriya and Rajputs. Few conscious rulers of India also tried to abolish this system, Akbar was one of them. Marathas entirely abolished this system in the state. Portuguese and French also tried to abolish this system in Goa and Chandranagar respectively. It was Raja Ram Mohan Roy who started his campaign against Sati practice. The Bengal Sati Regulation, or Regulation XVII (17), A.D. 1829 of the Bengal Code was a legal act promulgated in Bengal Presidency. In 1830, this regulation was also implemented in Madras and Bombay Presidencies. Then Governor-General Lord William Bentinck which banned the practice of sati system.

171.s: Sati system was abolished by –
171.x: The meaning of Sati is ‘holy and virtuous woman.’ In Hindu rituals, the marriage is considered as Sanskar which means ‘relation of spirits.’ The Brahmins of the 18th century used to believe that if a woman became Sati, seven generations of his husband will achieve heaven. It was quite famous among highly reputed Brahmins, Kshatriya and Rajputs. Few conscious rulers of India also tried to abolish this system, Akbar was one of them. Marathas entirely abolished this system in the state. Portuguese and French also tried to abolish this system in Goa and Chandranagar respectively. It was Raja Ram Mohan Roy who started his campaign against Sati practice. The Bengal Sati Regulation, or Regulation XVII (17), A.D. 1829 of the Bengal Code was a legal act promulgated in Bengal Presidency. In 1830, this regulation was also implemented in Madras and Bombay Presidencies. Then Governor-General Lord William Bentinck which banned the practice of sati system.

171.s: The enforcement of the Public Service was done in-

He introduced new policies regarding the personal business of British officers. He exclusively divided the jurisdiction of civil and judicial administration through “Cornwallis code” which later, in turn, transformed into civil services in India.

171.s: On the basis of alleged maladministration which Governor-General had taken the administration of Mysore state?

According to the wishes of the ‘Court of Directors,’ he adopted the policy of neutrality towards the Indian States. The chaos took such an ugly turn in Jaipur that there was an attack on British residents. But Lord Bentinck did not accept to interfere in that. Like this, he did not accept to interfere in Jodhpur, Bundi, Kota and Bhopal because of certain reasons. Excluding this policy, he annexed Mysore in 1831 A.D., State of Kurg (1834 A.D.), Kachhar in 1832 A.D.and Jayantia in 1835 A.D. because there was too much chaos in those states.

o: It banned propaganda by Christian Missionaries in
It made a financial allocation for the education of
It approved the development of a railway system in
174.x: The Charter Act, 1813 compelled the East India Company to assert the responsibility for the education of the Indians. It made a provision for an annual grant of a sum of 1 lakh rupees for the promotion of education in India.

174.s:
Consider the following statements about the Charter Acts:
1. The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly in India but retained its exclusive trade in tea and trade with China.
2. The Company's exclusive right to trade in tea and with China was abolished by the Charter Act of 1833.
3. The Charter Act of 1813 officially allowed Christian missionaries to enter India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
174.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the 1813 Act ended the general monopoly but kept the exclusive trade in tea and with China.
Statement 2: Correct: the Charter Act of 1833 removed the Company's remaining monopoly over tea and China trade.
Statement 3: Correct: under Evangelical pressure, the Charter Act of 1813 allowed missionaries to enter and preach.

174.s:
Consider the following statements about the Charter Acts of 1833 and 1853:
1. Under the Charter Act of 1833, laws made by the Governor-General-in-Council were called Acts.
2. The Charter Act of 1853 abolished the Directors' patronage and introduced open competition for civil-service recruitment.
3. The last Charter Act of the East India Company was the Charter Act of 1853.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
174.x:
Statement 1: Correct: from 1833 laws were called Acts instead of Regulations.
Statement 2: Correct: the 1853 Act abolished the patronage of the Court of Directors and introduced open competition.
Statement 3: Correct: the 1853 Act was the last; the Government of India Act of 1858 then transferred authority to the Crown.

174.s:
Consider the following statements about the Charter Act of 1833:
1. T. B. Macaulay was the first Law Member (the fourth member) of the Governor-General's Council under the Charter Act of 1833.
2. The first Law Commission (1834), which drafted the Indian Penal Code, was chaired by T.B. Macaulay.
3. The Charter Act of 1833 restored the law-making powers of the presidencies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
174.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the 1833 Act added a Law Member as the fourth member; Macaulay was the first to hold the post.
Statement 2: Correct: the first Law Commission was set up in 1834 under Macaulay and drafted the IPC.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the Charter Act of 1833 was the final step towards centralisation and made the Company purely administrative.

174.s: The statement, “The Company is an anomaly but it is part of a system where everything is an anomaly,” was made by Macaulay in the context of the:
174.x: Macaulay made this observation in his speech in the House of Commons on the Bill that became the Charter Act of 1833.
174.tq: Identify the Act from the context of the quoted political remark.
xs: Macaulay said "The Company is an **anomaly**..." in his Commons speech on the Bill that became the **Charter Act of 1833** — option **(3)**.
This was asked in UPPSC **2017**.
xa: The 1833 Act ended all **commercial functions** — the Company became purely administrative.
Macaulay became the **first Law Member** in **1834**.
His **Minute on Education** dates to **1835**.

174.s:
Consider the following statements about the Company's charter Acts:
1. Under the Charter Act of 1853, the two remaining new legislative members were not the Commander-in-Chief and the Law Member, but included the Chief Justice.
2. The Act of 1773 made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General of India.
3. The expression that the Indian territories of the East India Company were held "in trust" is associated with the Charter Act of 1813.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
174.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the two remaining members were not the Commander-in-Chief and the Law Member; they included the Chief Justice.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the 1773 Act made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General of Bengal, not of India.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the "in trust" expression is associated with the Charter Act of 1853, not 1813.

174.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
174.x: The Regulating Act was passed in 1773; Pitt's India Act was 1784, the Charter Act 1813 and the Government of India Act 1858.
n: The Regulating Act was enacted in 1773. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #131 · pp 234-235]
Pitt's India Act was enacted in 1784. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #131 · pp 234-235]
The Charter Act of 1813 ended the East India Company's monopoly in Indian trade. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #131 · pp 234-235]
The Government of India Act of 1858 ended the rule of the East India Company. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #131 · pp 234-235]
xa: The **1858** Act ended the **rule** of the **East India Company**.
**Charter Act 1813** ended the trade monopoly in India but kept **tea** and **China** trade, ended in **1833**.
The **Charter Act 1853** was the **last Charter Act**.
**1833**: **Lord William Bentinck** became the first **GG of India**.

174.s:
Consider the following statements about the Charter Act of 1833 and after:
1. Section 87 of the Charter Act of 1833 provided that no Indian should be barred from office on the grounds of religion, place of birth, descent or colour.
2. The territory separated from the Bengal Presidency and placed under the Agra Presidency by the Charter Act of 1833 was renamed in 1836 as the North-Western Provinces.
3. The Macaulay Committee on the Indian Civil Service was constituted in 1854.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
174.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Section 87 declared that religion, place of birth, descent or colour should not bar an Indian from office.
Statement 2: Correct: the separated territory was placed under the Agra Presidency in 1834 and renamed the North-Western Provinces in 1836.
Statement 3: Correct: the Macaulay Committee (1854) recommended competitive examinations in place of nomination.

174.s: Macaulay's Minute on Education is associated with the year:
174.x: Macaulay's Minute on Education was issued in 1835.
174.tq: Distinguish the year of the education minute from the nearby years of civil-service reform.
xs: Macaulay's **Minute on Education** dates to **1835** — option **(3)**.
**1800** is **Fort William College**; **1832** is **Ram Mohan Roy**'s demand; **1854** is the **Macaulay Committee** on the ICS.
xa: Macaulay was the **first Law Member (1834)**.
The **1813** Act had earlier given **Rs 1 lakh a year** — the first step towards State responsibility for education.

174.s: The Charter Act of 1813 provided an annual education grant of:
174.x: The grant was Rs 1,00,000 (1 lakh) a year, the first step towards State responsibility for education; Rs 10 lakh is a misprint.
xa: The **1813** Act also let **missionaries** enter India and propagate religion.
It made training of **civil servants** compulsory.
**Andhra:** it mandated public education as part of Company governance.

174.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Raja Ram Mohan Roy – demand for Indian participation in services, 1853
Charter Act of 1813 – open competitive examination for the ICS
Fort William College – established by Wellesley, 1806
174.x: Haileybury replaced Fort William College in 1806. Fort William College was set up in 1800, Roy's demand came in 1832 and open examinations came with the Charter Act of 1853.
xa: The **1813** Act made **civil-servant training** compulsory.
The **Macaulay Committee (1854)** preferred **university graduates**.
**Section 87** (1833): no Indian barred from office on religion, birth, descent or colour.

174.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Battle of Plassey
B. Battle of Buxar
C. Grant of Diwani rights
D. Regulating Act
174.x: Plassey was fought in 1757, Buxar in 1764, Diwani rights came in 1765 and the Regulating Act in 1773, giving A, B, C, D.
n: The Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #131 · pp 234-235]
The Battle of Buxar was fought in 1764. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #131 · pp 234-235]
The East India Company received Diwani rights in 1765. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #131 · pp 234-235]
The Regulating Act was enacted in 1773. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #131 · pp 234-235]
xs: The correct order is **A, B, C, D** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Battle of Plassey** **1757** → **Battle of Buxar** **1764** → **Diwani rights** **1765** → **Regulating Act** **1773**.
xa: After Buxar, **Shah Alam** granted the **Diwani** of Bengal, Bihar, Orissa to the Company.
**Pitt's India Act** followed in **1784**.
The **Charter Act 1813** ended the Company's monopoly in Indian trade; **1833** ended its commercial functions.

174.s: Who remarked about the East India Company that “The Company is an anomaly but it is part of a system where everything is an anomaly”?
174.x: Lord Thomas Babington Macaulay was a British politician and historian. He was the Law Member in the Supreme Council of India and the head of the Law Commission from 1834 to 1838 AD. He had prepared the manuscript of the famous Penal Law book 'The Indian Penal Code'. He had an important role in making English the official language and medium of education of India and European Literature, Philosophy and Science the goal of Indian education. Commenting on the policies of the East India Company. Macaulay said that "The company is an anomaly, but it is part of a system where everything is anomaly.

174.s: By which Act British Govt. abolished the monopoly of East India Company on trading of tea and sugar?
174.x: There were many consecutive Acts which were passed by British East India Company which as follows: Charter Act 1833: All commercial advantages and rights were completely abolished by the Charter Act, 1833. Now, Company had only administrative right on behalf of the British Crown.

174.s: What is not true in relation to the Charter Act, 1813?
o: It allowed Christian Missionaries to come to India for
It asserted the sovereignty of the British Crown over
This Act abolished the trade monopoly of the East
174.x: The monopoly of East India Company in India’s trade was abolished by the Charter Act of 1813. However they held the monopoly on the trade of Tea and trade with China.

174.s: Under which Act, Board of control was established –
174.x: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company’s trade monopoly except over Tea and trade with China. The Regulating Act of 1773 required the Company’s directors to present to the British Government all correspondence and documents pertaining to the administration of Company. Act of 1858 transferred the power from East India Company to British Crown to govern the administration and Pitt’s India Act 1784 set up a Board of Control in Britain to fully regulate the affairs of East India Company.

174.s: By which of the following regulation, British East India Company's trade monopoly in India was abolished?
174.x: The monopoly of East India Company in India’s trade was abolished by the Charter Act of 1813. However they held the monopoly on the trade of Tea and trade with China.

174.s: The monopoly of the East India Company in India’s trade was abolished in –
174.x: The monopoly of East India Company in India’s trade was abolished by the Charter Act of 1813. However they held the monopoly on the trade of Tea and trade with China.

174.s: By which Act, the British Parliament had abolished the monopoly of East India Company's trade in India except Tea and China trade?
174.x: The monopoly of East India Company in India’s trade was abolished by the Charter Act of 1813. However they held the monopoly on the trade of Tea and trade with China.

174.s: Which of the following Acts for the first time created a functioning Legislative Council in India?
174.x: A decisive step had been initiated in the separation of powers between the Executive and the Legislature by the Charter Act of 1853. It was the first time in India when the Legislative Council was established. The total number of the members in the Legislative Council was 12.

174.s: In which of the following year, almost the entire area of present Uttar Pradesh was separated from Bengal Presidency and placed under Agra Presidency?
174.x: The area of present-day Uttar Pradesh was acquired gradually by East India Company from the last quarter of 18th century to mid 19th century. This entire area was first placed with Bengal presidency, but in 1834, it was separated to form North-Western Provinces under Agra Presidency.

174.s: By which one of the following Acts was the Governor General of Bengal designated as the Governor General of India?
174.x: The Charter Act, 1833, was renewed on the condition that Company should abandon its trade entirely, both with India and China and permit Europeans to settle freely in India. The Company lost its monopoly in China and also the trade of tea which it enjoyed with the Charter Act of 1813. Governor- General of Bengal was made the Governor-General of British India with this Act, and all financial and administrative powers were centralized in the hands of Governor-Generalin-Council. The 4th member was not entitled to act as a member of the Council except for legislative purposes. A British member was appointed as a Law Member in the Governor-General’s Council. A first fourth person appointed as the Member of the Council was Lord Macaulay. Thus option (d) is the correct answer.

174.s: Which one of the following provisions was not made in the Charter Act of 1833?
o: The trading activities of the East India Company were
The designation of the supreme authority was to be
All law-making powers to be conferred on Governor-
An Indian was to be appointed as a Law Member of
174.x: The Charter Act, 1833, was renewed on the condition that Company should abandon its trade entirely, both with India and China and permit Europeans to settle freely in India. The Company lost its monopoly in China and also the trade of tea which it enjoyed with the Charter Act of 1813. Governor- General of Bengal was made the Governor-General of British India with this Act, and all financial and administrative powers were centralized in the hands of Governor-Generalin-Council. The 4th member was not entitled to act as a member of the Council except for legislative purposes. A British member was appointed as a Law Member in the Governor-General’s Council. A first fourth person appointed as the Member of the Council was Lord Macaulay. Thus option (d) is the correct answer.

174.s: Which Act provisioned competitive exam system for Civil Services?
174.x: The Charter Act, 1853 provided that the salary of the members of Board of Control, its Secretary and other Officers would be fixed by the Bri tish Government (British Crown) but the payments would be made out of the Com pany’s funds. The number of the Directors of the Court of Directors was re duced from 24 to 18 of whom 6 were to be nominated by the Crown. The Court of Directors was divested of its right to patronage and Company’s services were thrown open to competition and no dis crimination of any kind was to be made. A Committee with Macau lay was formed in the following year (1854) to give effect to the scheme of appointment in Civil Services through competition.

175.s:
Consider the following statements about the Permanent Settlement:
1. John Shore helped Cornwallis plan the Subsidiary Alliance.
2. The Permanent Settlement was introduced in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa in 1795.
3. Under the Sunset Law associated with the Permanent Settlement, an estate could be auctioned when the annual revenue was not paid by sunset on the due date.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
175.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: John Shore helped plan the Permanent Settlement, not the Subsidiary Alliance.
Statement 2: Incorrect: it was introduced in 1793, not 1795.
Statement 3: Correct: if the revenue was not paid by sunset of the due date, the estate could be auctioned.

175.s:
Consider the following statements about Ryotwari and Mahalwari origins:
1. The first experimental introduction of the Ryotwari system in the Madras Presidency took place in Baramahal.
2. The Mahalwari System was proposed in 1822 by Holt Mackenzie.
3. Baramahal came under Company control after the Third Mysore War in 1792.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
175.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the first experiment was in Baramahal, comprising areas such as Salem, Krishnagiri, Dharmapuri and Tiruvannamalai.
Statement 2: Correct: Holt Mackenzie proposed it in 1822; it was revised under Bentinck in 1833 with R.M. Bird.
Statement 3: Correct: Baramahal came under the Company in 1792.

175.s:
Assertion (A): Under the Ryotwari settlement, revenue was fixed on the land rather than directly on the crop produced.
Reason (R): Under the Ryotwari settlement, the assessment was ordinarily revised about every thirty years.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
175.x: Both are features of Ryotwari, but periodic revision does not explain why revenue was fixed on land.
xa: APPSC-GS **2018** asked these Ryotwari features.
Ryots had **proprietary rights** — sell, mortgage, gift, lease.
**Alice Thorner**: ryotwari **destroyed the village system** and isolated farmers.

175.s:
Consider the following statements about British land-revenue settlements:
1. Under the Mahalwari system, the unit of revenue assessment was the mahal (village or estate).
2. The Mahalwari system of land revenue was introduced mainly in the North-Western Provinces and parts of Punjab.
3. When the Permanent Settlement of 1793 was implemented in Andhra in 1802, the auction system was abolished and the tax was fixed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
175.x:
Statement 1: Correct: under Mahalwari the mahal was the unit, and revenue was collected through the headman or village community.
Statement 2: Correct: Mahalwari covered the North-Western Provinces (Agra-Oudh), parts of Punjab and Central India.
Statement 3: Correct: in Andhra, Cornwallis's 1793 Act was implemented in 1802; it abolished the auction system and fixed the tax.

175.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the Mahalwari-type arrangement is specifically associated with which area or areas?
175.x: The Mahalwari-type arrangement is placed in Nellore and Chittoor in the relevant regional account; in some accounts, Nellore alone is specifically mentioned.
175.tq: Use regional identification while avoiding confusion with named Zamindari estates.
xs: In Andhra, the Mahalwari-type arrangement is linked to **Nellore and Chittoor** — option **(2)**.
Some notes give **Nellore** only; there **village headmen** collected and remitted the tax.
**Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram, Nuzvid** were zamindaris under the Permanent Settlement.
xa: All three systems ran in Andhra: zamindari in the **Circars**, ryotwari in the **Ceded Districts**, mahalwari in **Nellore**.
Farmers depended on **village elders**.

175.s: Which statement about village-lease settlements in the Ceded Districts is correct?
o: They replaced ryotwari after Munro left in 1808 and continued until ryotwari was restored around 1820.
They preceded the 1792 Baramahal experiment and ended in 1799.
They were introduced only in the Northern Circars and never in the Ceded Districts.
They permanently replaced all forms of direct settlement in Rayalaseema.
175.x: Village-lease settlements, in which village headmen acted as lessees, replaced ryotwari in the Ceded Districts after Munro's departure from 1808 onward and lasted until about 1820.
175.tq: Track the temporary replacement and subsequent restoration of a revenue system.
xs: **Village-lease settlements** replaced ryotwari after Munro left (**1808** onward) until ryotwari was **restored around 1820** — option **(1)**.
Village **headmen** acted as lessees.
They were in the **Ceded Districts**, not the Circars, and were not permanent.
xa: A **2018** PYQ stem gave the Andhra ryotwari date as **1808**; the answer is still **Munro**.
General Madras adoption came in **1820** under Munro as Governor.

175.s:
Consider the following statements about effects of colonial land revenue:
1. Rigid land revenue demands frequently pushed ryots towards moneylenders because revenue had to be paid in cash even when crops failed.
2. The need to pay land revenue in cash encouraged the cultivation of commercial crops such as indigo, cotton, opium and jute.
3. Merchant-landlords emerged in Zamindari areas, while moneylender-landlords emerged in Ryotwari and Mahalwari areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
175.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the inflexible cash demand continued during crop failures, forcing ryots to borrow from Mahajans.
Statement 2: Correct: cash revenue demands pushed peasants to grow commercial crops such as indigo, cotton, opium and jute.
Statement 3: Correct: merchant-landlords became prominent in Zamindari areas and moneylender-landlords in Ryotwari and Mahalwari areas.

175.s:
Consider the following statements about Ryotwari and Mahalwari systems:
1. Ryotwari revenue was not permanently fixed at a low and unchangeable rate.
2. Under the Ryotwari and Mahalwari systems, the revenue assessment was periodically revised.
3. Under the Mahalwari System, revenue was collected by the individual ryot.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
175.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Ryotwari suffered from over-assessment, inadequate records and unclear boundaries; its revenue was periodically revised and often heavy.
Statement 2: Correct: revenue was fixed forever under the Permanent Settlement but periodically revised under Ryotwari and Mahalwari.
Statement 3: Incorrect: under Mahalwari the lambardar (village headman) collected the revenue.

175.s:
Consider the following statements about British land-revenue settlements:
1. Under the Mahalwari System, default in revenue payment made the village collectively liable.
2. Alice Thorner criticised the Ryotwari system on the ground that it created a permanent landlord class in the Northern Circars.
3. The Permanent Settlement was not introduced in Madras and Coorg.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
175.x:
Statement 1: Correct: under Mahalwari the village was collectively liable; under Ryotwari the cultivator's land could be seized.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Alice Thorner argued that Ryotwari destroyed the village system and isolated farmers from the government.
Statement 3: Correct: Madras and Coorg came under Ryotwari, not the Permanent Settlement.

175.s:
Consider the following statements about British land-revenue settlements:
1. Under the Mahalwari system, the revenue relationship was between the Government and the village or mahal.
2. The Ryotwari Settlement is associated with Thomas Munro and Alexander Read.
3. The Ryotwari system was first begun, from 1792, in the Ceded Districts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
175.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Permanent Settlement dealt with the zamindar, Ryotwari with the ryot and Mahalwari with the village or mahal.
Statement 2: Correct: Ryotwari is linked to Thomas Munro and Alexander Read.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Ryotwari began in Baramahal from 1792, not in the Ceded Districts.

175.s:
Consider the following statements about land revenue and tenancy:
1. The initial demand in the first Ryotwari experiment was 50% of the estimated produce.
2. The Bengal Tenancy Act of 1885 dealt with the extension of Ryotwari in Madras.
3. Thomas Munro was the first Principal Collector of Rayalaseema and established a direct ryot–state relationship there.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
175.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the first Ryotwari demand was 50% of the estimated produce, not 30%.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885 dealt with the rights of landlords and tenants in Bengal and Bihar.
Statement 3: Correct: Munro established the direct ryot–state relationship through ryotwari.

175.s: Which of the following pairs (settlement – approximate share of British-held area) is correctly matched?
175.x: The Permanent Settlement covered about 19%, Ryotwari about 51% and Mahalwari about 30%, so Ryotwari and Mahalwari together covered about 81%.
n: The Permanent Settlement covered approximately 19% of the British-occupied area. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
The Ryotwari Settlement covered approximately 51% of the British-occupied area. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
The Mahalwari Settlement covered approximately 30% of the British-occupied area. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
xa: Mahalwari areas: **NWP (Agra-Oudh region), Punjab, Central India**.
Permanent Settlement areas: **Bengal, Bihar, Odisha**, **Varanasi**.
Ryotwari areas: **Madras**, parts of **Bombay**, **Assam**, **Coorg**.

175.s:
Consider the following statements about the Permanent Settlement:
1. The Permanent Settlement initially began as a quinquennial settlement.
2. The sale of many old zamindari estates under the Permanent Settlement contributed to the emergence of a new landed class of urban merchants and moneylenders.
3. Absentee landlordism, sub-infeudation and rack-renting were effects of the Permanent Settlement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
175.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: it began as a ten-year (decennial) settlement, not a quinquennial one.
Statement 2: Correct: estates lost for arrears were purchased by urban merchants and moneylenders, creating a new landed class.
Statement 3: Correct: these, along with peasants reduced to tenants-at-will, were effects of the Permanent Settlement.

175.s: Under the zamindari arrangement, the gains from agriculture went mainly to the:
175.x: Under the zamindari system, gains from agriculture went to the zamindars, not to the Company.
xa: Effects: **absentee landlordism**, **sub-infeudation**, **rack-renting**.
Zamindars moved to cities like **Calcutta** and left collection to agents.

175.s:
Consider the following statements about the Permanent Settlement:
1. According to the commonly cited distribution of rent under the Permanent Settlement, the zamindar retained 1/10.
2. A fixed revenue demand under the Permanent Settlement prevented the Company from receiving later increases from agricultural prices.
3. In Coastal Andhra, zamindars of the Zamindari areas paid the Company peshkash.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
175.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the commonly cited distribution gave the state 10/11 and the zamindar 1/11.
Statement 2: Correct: ensuring later price gains for the Company was not a rationale; a fixed demand actually prevented the Company from receiving them.
Statement 3: Correct: coastal lands were divided into Haveli and Zamindari areas, whose zamindars paid peshkash.

175.s:
Consider the following statements about colonial land-revenue settlements:
1. The Madras Inam Commission, which investigated titles to rent-free inam lands, was constituted in 1822.
2. The three major British land-revenue settlements made land a transferable commodity.
3. The criticism that the State became the 'ultimate landlord' was directed at the Ryotwari System.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
175.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the Madras Inam Commission was constituted in 1858.
Statement 2: Correct: the settlements made land transferable, created a loyal landlord class and fed rural indebtedness.
Statement 3: Correct: critics held that under Ryotwari the state became the ultimate landlord.

175.s: Who suppressed the Palegars of Rayalaseema?
175.x: As Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts, Thomas Munro suppressed the Palegars of Rayalaseema.

175.s: Who was known as the first Principal Collector of Rayalaseema?
175.x: Sir Thomas Munro served as the first Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts (Rayalaseema region), where he developed the Ryotwari land revenue system, significantly shaping subsequent British land revenue policy across Madras Presidency.

175.s:
Consider the following statements about Thomas Munro:
1. In the Andhra region, Thomas Munro first introduced Ryotwari in 1802 in the Ceded Districts.
2. Thomas Munro's headquarters as the first Collector of the Ceded Districts was located at Pattikonda.
3. Early in his career, Thomas Munro served in the Baramahal as assistant to Holt Mackenzie.

Statement 2: Incorrect: Munro's headquarters was at Anantapur, not Pattikonda.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Munro was assistant to Alexander Read, not Holt Mackenzie, in the Baramahal.

175.s:
Consider the following statements about Thomas Munro and Andhra:
1. Sir Thomas Munro, who died of cholera at Pattikonda in 1827, was buried at Anantapur.
2. Campbell assisted Thomas Munro in suppressing the Palegars in the Ceded Districts before the introduction of Ryotwari settlement.
3. The land-revenue pattern in Andhra was Ryotwari in the Circars, Mahalwari in Rayalaseema and Zamindari in Nellore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
175.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Munro was buried at Gooty; Anantapur was his headquarters as Collector.
Statement 2: Correct: Munro suppressed the Palegars with officer Campbell's assistance before bringing in Ryotwari.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the pattern was Zamindari in the Circars, Ryotwari in the Ceded Districts and Mahalwari in Nellore.

175.s:
Consider the following statements about Ryotwari and Rayalaseema:
1. Under the Ryotwari system, the ryot had the right to sell, mortgage, gift or lease the land so long as the assessment was paid.
2. Under the Ryotwari system, occasional remission or reduction of revenue was possible after a bad harvest.
3. Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy's revolt in the 1840s is associated with looting the treasury at Kovela Kuntla.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
175.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the ryot held proprietary rights as long as the assessment was paid.
Statement 2: Correct: Ryotwari gave no automatic exemption, but occasional remission or reduction was possible.
Statement 3: Correct: during the Kurnool Polygar revolt, Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy looted the treasury at Kovela Kuntla.

o: Holt Mackenzie – devised the Mahalwari system

175.s:
Consider the following statements about land revenue in Andhra:
1. The Regulations of 1799 and 1812 empowered zamindars to seize the property of tenants under the Permanent Settlement.
2. Thomas Munro's administrative philosophy favoured direct contact with cultivators, no intermediaries and communication in fluent Telugu.

175.x:

Statement 3: Correct: after 1802 the mootahdars held the mootahs in the manner of proprietary estates.

Consider the following statements about land settlements in Andhra:
1. In the Madras Presidency, the Northern Circars were mainly under the zamindari settlement.
2. The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948 provided for the full conversion of Zamindari estates into Ryotwari holdings in the Madras Presidency.

175.x: Alexander Read with Thomas Munro first introduced the Ryotwari system of revenue collection in Baramahal.

175.s: The tendency for increased litigation was visible after the introduction of the land settlement system of Lord Cornwallis in 1793. The reason for this is normally traced to which of the following provisions?
o: Making Zamindar's position stronger vis-a-vis the ryot
Making East India Company an overlord of Zamindars
175.x: The judicial reforms introduced by Cornwallis, particularly after the implementation of the land settlement system, led to a significant increase in litigation. This was largely due to the abolition of court fees, which made access to courts easier for all sections of society. Additionally, the expansion of the right to appeal encouraged more people to pursue legal remedies, resulting in a sharp rise in the number of court cases.

175.s: The English introduced the Ryotwari System for the first time in
175.x: Ryotwari System was a method of revenue collection in British India. It was prevalent in most of Southern India is the standard system of Madras Presidency. The system was devised by Alexander Reed and Thomas Munro. It was introduced by Thomas Munro when he was the Governor of Madras.

175.s:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as
Reason (R) :
Assertion (A) : The British Government introduced different land revenue system in different part of India.
Reason (R) : It led to create different classes in Indian peasantry.
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct
175.x: British government followed different land revenue systems in different parts of India. These systems were: Permanent Settlement, Ryotwari & Mahalwari. Permanent Settlement was introduced in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha & Varanasi of U.P. Under this system around 19% area of entire British India was included. Ryotwari (approx. 51% area) system was in Madras, some parts of Mumbai, Assam, Coorg. Mahalwari (around 30% of the area) system around was in U.P, Central Province, Punjab. Hence, it is clear that because of this, different classes were created in Indian peasantry. Hence, option (a) is correct.

175.s: Who introduced the system of Mahalwari Settlement in Bengal?
o: More than one of the above
175.x: Mahalwari system was devised by Holt Mackenzie (then the territorial secretary of Board of Revenue) in 1822 A.D. in the Bengal Presidency. Under this system, the land revenue was collected from the farmers by treating whole village as single unit called 'Mahal'. The revenue was not fixed but revised periodically.

175.s: Who started Ryotwari system?
175.x: Ryotwari System was the second system of collection of land revenue after Permanent Settlement. Thomas Munro and Captain Alexander Read were the founders of this system. This system was first introduced in Baramahal district (Tamil Nadu). After that, this system was introduced in Madras, Assam, Coorg and some areas of Bombay. In Ryotwari System, the ownership rights were transferred to the peasants. British government collected taxes directly from the peasants around 51% of British occupied Indian area was included in this system. The high rate of taxes and strictness during collection became a significant cause of struggle between money lenders and peasants.

175.s: Who among the following said "The Ryotwari is a system which has always prevailed in India"?
175.x: Ryotwari system was started by Thomas Munro and Alexander Read in the Baramahal district of Tamilnadu. According to this system the Ryots were given the ownership and rights to occupy the lands and they were required to pay the revenue directly to the government. Thomas Munro said regarding this system that "The Ryotwari is a system which has always prevailed in India."

175.s: Sir Thomas Munro was Governor of Madras during years
175.x: Sir Thomas Munro was governor of Madras during 1820- 1827 A.D. He is regarded as the father of Ryotwari System in India in which the taxes of agriculture land were directly collected from the ryots (owner of the land).

175.s: Under the Permanent Settlement, 1793, the Zamindars were required to issue pattas to the farmers which were not issued by many of the Zamindars. The reason was:
o: the Zamindars were trusted by the farmers
there was no officials check upon the Zamindars
it was the responsibility of the British government
the farmers were not interested in getting pattas
175.x: The reason for not issuing pattas by many Zamindars was that there was no official check on Zamindars in permanent settlement of 1793 A.D. They were only required to give 10/11th part of the revenue collection to the officials.

175.s: The system under which the peasant himself owns the land and is responsible for payment of land revenue to the Government is known as :
175.x: Under the Ryotwari system, the farmer himself is the owner of the land and is held responsible for the payment of land revenue to the government.

175.x: In 1793 A.D., Lord Cornwallis introduced Permanent Settlement which in turn provided many rights to landlords. By the 19th century, the demand for land increased and hence landlords increased the rent of the land which resulted in a revolt by peasants. During this time, the government of Bengal introduced the Bengal and Bihar Tenancy Act 1885, which described the rights of landlords and tenants.

175.s:
With reference to Ryotwari Settlement, consider the following statements
1. The rent was paid directly by the peasants to the government.
2. The government gave the Pattas to the Ryots.
3. The lands were surveyed and assessed before being taxed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
175.x: All statements are correct: Under the Ryotwari Settlement (Munro System), the cultivator (ryot) was recognised as the owner of his land, subject to paying land revenue. The cultivators were registered and issued pattas. They were permitted to sell, lease, mortgage or transfer the right to land. Revenue settlement was directly made with the ryot. The land was surveyed carefully and separately before determining the revenue assessment. The settlement was periodically revised after 20 to 30 years, when the revenue demand was usually raised, taking into account changes in grain prices, marketing opportunities, irrigation facilities, etc. Ryotwari Settlement was introduced in parts of the Madras and Bombay Presidencies, Assam, and Burma.

175.s: The Ryotwari system was first implemented in :
175.x: In Ryotwari System, every registered holder of land is recognised as a proprietor of land and is held responsible for direct payment of land revenue to the state. In the Madras presidency, the first land revenue settlement was made in the Baramahal district after its acquisition was done by the company in 1792 A.D. Alexander Read assisted by Thomas Munro fixed the state demand on the basis of 50% of the estimated produce of the fields. Later on when Thomas Munro became Governor of Madras (1820-27 A.D.), he extended the Ryotwari system to all parts of the province (except the permanently settled areas). A Permanent Settlement was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793 A.D.
